Wider Sports News.title: How creators changed sports media with access, not airtime
Wider Sports News.summary: As athletes and rights holders open up more direct access to fans, creators are reshaping sports media by building trust, reaching new audiences and challenging traditional ideas of who holds authority. The post How creators changed sports media with access, not airtime appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Judging this year’s Sports Journalism Awards was an eye opener as it gave a clear indication of what was actually winning. A Bundesliga YouTube show took a broadcast category, a creator-exclusive award went to a channel built entirely around access not airtime. A newcomer prize went to a football podcast with zero broadcast pedigree. And while the traditional players were in the running, they weren’t running away with it.

It also clearly shows that sports fans aren’t just turning to the traditional print, web and broadcast outlets anymore.. They’re getting their news from creators, presenters and former players who talk to them like people, not audiences.

Wider Sports News.title: The business of the US Open: Record prize money, new leadership and an US$800m renovation
Wider Sports News.summary: As this year’s tournament begins with a record US$108m prize fund, SportsPro breaks down what fuels one of the most lucrative events in tennis. The post The business of the US Open: Record prize money, new leadership and an US$800m renovation appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The US Open is the final Grand Slam tournament of the year and among the most lucrative events on the tennis calendar. Loud, vibrant and festival-like, the event mirrors the character of New York City, a far cry from the manicured lawns and traditions of Wimbledon. Unlike its British counterpart, which is known for keeping partner branding to a minimum, the US Open is defined by bold sponsorship activations and star-studded musical performances.

Yet tennis remains the main attraction, with this year’s storylines including Carlos Alcaraz returning from a four-month wrist injury to defend his title and Aryna Sabalenka chasing a third consecutive crown. There will also be plenty of attention on the Williams sisters, who have been handed a wild card to play in the women’s doubles.

Rugby.title: ‘Not always easy to understand’: Bok scrum coach responds to accusations
Rugby.summary: South Africa scrum coach Daan Human has emphatically asserted that he has "never coached" his side to walk around in the scrum, adding that it is "not ideal for us".
Rugby.body:
South Africa scrum coach Daan Human has emphatically asserted that he has “never coached” his side to walk around in the scrum, adding that it is “not ideal for us”. Speaking to the media in the wake of the Springboks’ second Test victory over the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, Human defended his pack in light of accusations made by New Zealand boss Dave Rennie over alleged underhanded tactics in the scrum.

“The scrums were better tonight,” Rennie said after his side fell 33-26 in Cape Town to leave the four-match series level. “I think Angus was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep the hookers in the same spacing.

Rugby.title: What is Australia’s first-choice team and how far does depth go, a year out from RWC27?
Rugby.summary: Les Kiss still has to settle on his optimum back-row combination, midfield pairing and back-up half-backs.
Rugby.body:
It was a really important win for Australia in Argentina, their fourth straight in 2026 and the first time they’ve enjoyed a streak this long since beating Portugal in their final match of RWC2023 – the end of the season to forget – and then winning their first three Tests under Joe Schmidt in 2024.

Schmidt’s Wallabies never won four in a row, but Les Kiss’s side can this Saturday in Mendoza. If they succeed, it would also see their overall streak – taking into account the win over Italy in Schmidt’s last Test – equal Dave Rennie’s run of five straight wins in 2021.

Rugby.title: Where are the Yaras one week ahead of the WXV Global Series Challenger?
Rugby.summary: Two wins over South Africa 'A', 63 points scored and 31 conceded and a big momentum boost for the Yaras ahead of their first WXV Global Series Challenger participation.
Rugby.body:
Two wins over South Africa ‘A’, 63 points scored and 31 conceded and a big momentum boost for the Yaras ahead of their first WXV Global Series Challenger campaign. There’s no denying that Brazil has taken another step in their development since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, showcasing strong foundations in their game plan and a deeper squad better equipped to cope with the demands of any kind.

With the conclusion of the South Africa ‘A’ series, Brazil has recorded five wins – and just one defeat – since Guilherme Coghetto took charge of the women’s national team and programme. A more than promising sign ahead of their clashes against Hong Kong China, Netherlands and Spain.

Rugby.title: Spain boosted as award-winning scrum-half returns for WXV Global Series Challenger
Rugby.summary: Spain head coach Régis Sonnes has named the Las Leonas squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for WXV Global Series Challenger.
Rugby.body:
Spain head coach Régis Sonnes has named the Las Leonas squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for WXV Global Series Challenger. There is a Test rugby return for Anne Fernández de Corres on the cards. The scrum-half has not represented her country in 15-a-side rugby since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, and represented the ACT Brumbies in Super Rugby Women’s earlier this year. During her time in Canberra she was named Helen Taylor Award for Women’s Player of the Year by the team.

Additionally, there are welcome returns to the squad for Alba Capell and Carmen Castellucci, who both missed the majority of the 2025/26 season with long-term injuries. Ahead of her time in Australia, the 28-year-old told RugbyPass: “By leaving my comfort zone, I have experienced some growth and self-development.

Rugby.title: 'They did not see the best of me': Vainah Ubisi vows to make her mark against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: Vainah Ubisi has mixed memories of the Springboks' Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 campaign.
Rugby.body:
Vainah Ubisi has mixed memories of the Springboks‘ Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 campaign. On one hand, it was an historic occasion for South Africa as their women’s side reached the quarter-final stage of the tournament for the first time. On the other, she did not perform to the lofty standard she has set.

The 23-year-old lock, who has played in 26 Test matches already in her career, saw her preparation for last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup curtailed by a knee injury. Instead of being utilised as a starter, Ubisi was used from the bench on three occasions. Including their quarter-final exit to the Black Ferns at Exeter’s Sandy Park.

Rugby.summary: George Furbank has been lost to Harlequins and James Ramm's versatility will be missed from the back three, but otherwise Saints have a largely settled and consistent group who know each other's game inside and out.
Rugby.body:
Despite missing club captain George Furbank for large chunks of the season and being hit harder by England call-ups more than most, Northampton won back the PREM trophy in 2025/26 and are short odds to be crowned champions of England for a third time in four years.

Rugby.title: Amy du Plessis: 'The game you love doesn’t always love you back'
Rugby.summary: Some of the most moving social media content at Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 featured tearful Black Ferns bidding farewell to grief-stricken centre Amy du Plessis.
Rugby.body:
Some of the most moving social media content at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 featured tearful Black Ferns bidding farewell to grief-stricken centre Amy du Plessis. In the opening 54-8 win against Spain in York, she injured her shoulder after falling awkwardly in a tackle. She was due to return for the quarter-final agains South Africa, the country of her birth, but did not recover in time.

This weekend she has unfinished business in the historic first Test between the Black Ferns and Springbok Women at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg. “The game you love doesn’t always love you back,” Du Plessis told RugbyPass.

Rugby.title: Forget McZanno or McRizz; Tom Hooper has just blown that experiment out of the water
Rugby.summary: The debate about having McReight and Tizzano on the field together is moot, not to mention the conversation surrounding what the duo should be called.
Rugby.body:
There are a few key reasons why conventional No.7s are now an endangered species at Test level, and it is seeing selection pictures change course. The main reason for this move is that the breakdown turnover, also called the pilfer, or what is occasionally known as the jackal, is now a skill expected to be performed by several players, not just the player wearing the No.7 jersey.

Hookers with their athletic but stocky build traditionally have become a second pilfer option, but that mould never stopped All Blacks great Sam Whitelock from being a clutch jackaler.

Rugby.title: No one bought the Springboks' set piece charade
Rugby.summary: The mirage that was sold to the South African public was that this would be a one-sided series at scrum time. Those expectations were set on a false premise during those first 50 minutes.
Rugby.body:
The first Test in Johannesburg featured the most lopsided scrum in rugby history, with South Africa seemingly dominating the All Blacks on every feed. It looked like a masterclass in scrummaging and a demonstration of a weapon of mass destruction.

Once the reserve front rows came on, the scrum stabilised with no advantage to the Springboks for the final half hour. Then head coach Dave Rennie revealed that Ethan de Groot played through illness, coming down sick the night before.

Rugby.title: 'One-week wonders': Dave Rennie's All Blacks on World Rankings shortlist
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' stay at the top of the World Rugby Men's Rankings only lasted one week after they fell to a 33-26 defeat to South Africa in the second Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series in Cape Town on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Only one week after climbing to No.1 in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings, the All Blacks were removed from their lofty perch by South Africa as a result of the Springboks’ 33-26 win in Cape Town in the second Test of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

In falling from grace so swiftly, they became only the fifth team in the 23-year history of the rankings to have the very briefest of stays as the world’s best team. Not that Dave Rennie cares a jot, he’s publicly said so.

Rugby.title: World Rugby statement: November's Nations Cup fixtures
Rugby.summary: World Rugby has confirmed the fixture schedule for the second phase of the inaugural Nations Cup, with 18 matches to be played across Europe and Hong Kong between November 6 and 21.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby has confirmed the fixture schedule for the second phase of the inaugural Nations Cup, with 18 matches to be played across Europe and Hong Kong between November 6 and 21.

Pool A consists of Canada, Chile, Samoa, Tonga, Uruguay and the USA. Pool B includes Georgia, Hong Kong China, Portugal, Romania, Spain and Zimbabwe. Teams play every nation from the opposite pool across the two international windows. At the conclusion of the six-round schedule, the team finishing top of each pool will be crowned inaugural Nations Cup champions.

Rugby.title: Where does Cheslin Kolbe rank in the elite goalkicking wingers' club?
Rugby.summary: Cheslin Kolbe has been perfect from the kicking tee during Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series with New Zealand, nailing four from four in the first Test and seven from seven in the second
Rugby.body:
Cheslin Kolbe has been perfect from the kicking tee during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series with New Zealand, nailing four from four in the first Test and seven from seven in the second. Not bad for a player who’d only been a bit-part Test goalkicker up until then.

Due to the presence of Handrè Pollard and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu in the team, Kolbe did not take a single shot at goal in 2024 and 2025, and was only called upon seven times during the southern hemisphere section of this year’s Nations Championship (succeeding with five kicks). That said, he has found his rhythm with his club Suntory Sungoliath in Japan’s Rugby League One, finishing this season as top points scorer

Rugby.title: 'The All Blacks are asking South Africa all the questions that matter'
Rugby.summary: The world champions maintain a vice-like grip on the set-piece, but New Zealand are hurting them in different ways as the Greatest Rivalry series hots up.
Rugby.body:
A fisherman always spots another fisherman from afar. Giants in any field of human endeavour usually share the same competitive instincts and goals, but they rarely occupy the same space. There may be an unspoken recognition of the same traits and ambitions, an imperceptible tip of the hat from one bank to the other, but the river moves on swiftly and the focus returns, inevitably, to the float bobbing on the water. The next catch.

The two biggest pescadores of either era in rugby, amateur or professional, have been locked in silent combat for 105 years, with the just the occasional silent nod to the accomplishments of the other punctuating the torrential surge of the greatest rivalry. There have been seven prize World Cup catches between the two, with the last tussle between the twin titans decided by one single point in Paris.

Rugby.summary: Sale have gone full bore in their selection, handing debuts to England internationals Courtney Lawes, Joe Marchant and Alex Lozowski.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson has done ‘a Rassie Erasmus’ and gone early in naming his team for Sunday’s PREM Rugby Cup opener at home to Bath. While some clubs will treat the first batch of Cup games as a chance to give fringe players a run out, Sale have gone full bore in their selection, handing debuts to England internationals Courtney Lawes, Joe Marchant and Alex Lozowski.

Loose forward Lawes and centre/wing Marchant were big-name signings from France, while fly-half/centre Lozowski returns north having made a name for himself at Leeds before enjoying a stellar career at Wasps and then Saracens.

Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has hailed Eben Etzebeth as “probably the best Springbok of all time” after the veteran lock produced a towering response to the pressure surrounding his form in Saturday’s series-levelling 33-26 victory over the All Blacks in Cape Town.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has hailed Eben Etzebeth as “probably the best Springbok of all time” after the veteran lock produced a towering response to the pressure surrounding his form in Saturday’s series-levelling 33-26 victory over the All Blacks in Cape Town.

The 34-year-old racked up a match-leading 18 tackles, two of which were dominant, as the world champions levelled the series with the All Blacks, but perhaps his work at the lineout was his most decisive contribution, as he terrorised the visitors’ throw at the front of the lineout.

Rugby.title: Losing Gloucester captaincy was 'brutal'
Rugby.summary: Gloucester's Lewis Ludlow on losing the captaincy last season, his two England caps, and chasing a record in his upcoming testimonial season.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester flanker Lewis Ludlow says it was "brutal" to lose the club captaincy last August and he would "take it back tomorrow" if offered. Ludlow has played more than 250 games for the Cherry and Whites and his time as skipper between 2020 and 2025 makes him the longest-serving captain in the club's history.

However, the 31-year-old was replaced by Tomos Williams in the role for the 2025-26 season, although the Welshman signed for Saracens this summer. "It was brutal," Ludlow told BBC Radio Gloucestershire about being told he was no longer captain.

Rugby.title: Pouri Rakete-Stones: Newcastle's Maori strongman with Red Bull flair and England ambitions
Rugby.summary: The former Hurricane is English-qualified, and eager to make a splash as Red Bull's fascinating overhaul of Newcastle takes shape.
Rugby.body:
In Te reo Maori, the word ‘Pouri’ tends to carry a solemn resonance. It often conveys a sense of sorrow or sadness; the echo of some grave event etched in community lore. In the Rakete-Stones family, it bears no such gloom. Certainly, the colourful and rambunctious prop who has signed up to join Newcastle’s Red Bull revolution is nothing like the sincere translation of his moniker.

Two recent Pouris came before the straggly-haired strongman from Napier. His father, Pouri senior, and his great-uncle, a redoubtable Maori who in later life, has retreated to the wilderness of New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Why Peter Lakai could be the All Blacks' ace up the sleeve for the third Test
Rugby.summary: Blindside flanker is one position Dave Rennie and the selectors have continually tinkered with while being steadfast on Savea at No.8 and Luke Jacobson at openside.
Rugby.body:
Blindside flanker is one position Dave Rennie and the selectors have continually tinkered with while being steadfast on Savea at No.8 and Luke Jacobson at openside. Peter Lakai had the first crack against France, before Wallace Sititi against Italy, and Tupou Vaa’i against Ireland. Simon Parker came into the starting line-up for his first game of the year in the second Test as Tupou Vaa’i moved back to lock.

Vaa’i had less impact than in the first Test, crucially coughing up a kick restart that led to a cheap three points for the Springboks. The lineout calls were also off, with the All Blacks attempting to throw to the middle and back too much, which were disrupted by Eben Etzebeth and Pieter-Steph du Toit. If the Boks didn’t pinch it, they often knocked it down, creating loose ball.

Rugby.summary: "Roger leaves with our gratitude and best wishes, and he will always be welcomed back to Chiefs HQ and region”
Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: All Blacks need to knock the front door down first
Rugby.summary: If there’s an area of concern for me, it’s in the All Blacks’ desperation to go around the Springboks. To shovel the ball across, no matter what pressure that puts on a teammate.
Rugby.body:
If that’s the standard, the All Blacks aren’t far off it. I’m not remotely discouraged by New Zealand’s 33-26 loss to South Africa in Cape Town. Yes, the lineout is under pressure and, of course, you’d like the All Blacks to be better at catching high balls. But I feared the Springboks could dish out a hiding in this match and they didn’t.

As I’ve indicated many times, this is a development tour for the All Blacks. It’s about exposing players such as Ruben Love and seeing how they cope. This is a team that’s rebuilding. The past standards of excellence don’t apply here, because of how far the All Blacks have fallen in recent times.

Rugby.title: Jason Ryan weighs in on Boks' late changes and Rassie's 'friendly fire' outburst
Rugby.summary: The scrum has been a dramatic feature of the Greatest Rivalry tour on numerous fronts, with Saturday evening's Cape Town Test adding yet another twist in the tale.
Rugby.body:
The scrum has been a dramatic feature of the Greatest Rivalry tour on numerous fronts, with Saturday evening’s Cape Town Test adding yet another twist in the tale. The game started with a selection curveball from Rassie Erasmus, who swapped his starting front row with his bench unit at the last minute. The coach later explained the move as a response to the conditions, which were drier than what was forecast earlier in the week.

After the game ended, Erasmus took exception to his All Blacks counterpart Dave Rennie expressing further concern over South Africa’s scrum tactics, accusing the hosts of making a late side-step before setting the scrum to overload the Kiwi tighthead props.

Rugby.title: SANZAAR team of the week: Springboks lead combined XV
Rugby.summary: Test Rugby at it's finest. Test two of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series and the opening exchange in the Flight Centre series between Argentina and Australia offered a contrasting set of fixtures.
Rugby.body:
Test rugby at its finest. That is what rugby fans were treated to on Saturday’s bumper back-to-back set of contrasting Southern Hemisphere series. In Cape Town, Rassie Erasmus’s world champions held the All Blacks at arm’s length without ever looking entirely home and dry to level Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series at one a piece. To their credit, Dave Rennie’s side all but nullified the Springbok set-piece, despite ultimately falling short of landing what would have been a near-knockout blow in the series.

The legality of the Springbok scrum dominated the post-match exchanges between the two coaches, with Rennie’s pre-match messaging appearing to filter through to the officials.

Rugby.title: What Rassie’s risky business says about the Springboks
Rugby.summary: An Airlink Embraer E195 jet has no business skimming the roof of a sports stadium. Nor does a rugby coach have much business changing his team less...
Rugby.body:
An Airlink Embraer E195 jet has no business skimming the roof of a sports stadium. Nor does a rugby coach have much business changing his team less than 48 hours before kick-off, let alone replacing an entire front row an hour before the opening whistle. Yet both things happened in Cape Town.

South Africans do things differently when the stakes rise. Risk is not always a red line. Sometimes it is an invitation to create something special. The planes passed perilously close to the stadium. Rassie Erasmus’s side then staged a narrow escape of their own, absorbing an All Blacks comeback before holding on for a seven-point victory that kept the series alive. In South African rugby, the result is often its own absolution.

Rugby.title: Quinn Tupaea on facing early Springboks' onslaught and All Blacks being 'right there'
Rugby.summary: All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea says the team expected the early Springboks onslaught they received, revealing they trained all week on how to get back momentum.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea says the team expected the early Springboks onslaught they received, revealing they trained all week on how to get back momentum. Right from the first exit the Springboks went into a strong maul, then played their powerful forwards around the corner off Cobus Reinach until the halfback spotted an opportunity for Jesse Kriel to crash over a little bit wider.

The home side were up 7-0 after just two minutes, something that Tupaea says didn’t phase the All Blacks with a lot of belief in their own game. “It was something we expected. Just had to reset and go again. Obviously, nail the kick off and then get into our set piece. If I remember right, we parked up down there for a little bit after that. So yeah, took some positives from it, I guess,” Tupaea told media post-game.

Moments earlier, at the All Blacks press conference, Rennie had shared his initial thoughts on the scrum contest and how it was refereed by Angus Gardner. “The scrums were better tonight,” he said. “I think Angus was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep the hookers in the same spacing.

Rugby.title: ‘No excuse’: Simon Parker fronts up after tense Springboks defeat
Rugby.summary: Parker, who started his first Test match under Dave Rennie against the Springboks, was honest in his reflection of the contest.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks loose-forward enforcer Simon Parker has reflected on the Springboks levelling Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series at DHL Stadium in Cape Town. Rassie Erasmus’ side didn’t allow the All Blacks to find their way into the contest, stifling the visitors in Cape Town.

Leroy Carter and Will Jordan dotted down late to mount a comeback for the All Blacks, but it was too little, too late, as Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks held on. The Chiefs No.6 was chosen over the likes of Peter Lakai, Wallace Sititi, Ethan Blackadder, and Patrick Tuipulotu for a starting jumper in Cape Town, after featuring off the bench in the first Test match at Ellis Park.

World champions South Africa delivered a powerful first-half performance as they edged past New Zealand and levelled 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series at 1-1 with two Tests to play.

Rugby.summary: "They got a couple down our end, especially late in the piece, and Cheslin Kolbe was able to kick those. So we'll have a look at that.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie believes his side have plenty of positives to take out of their narrow defeat at the hands of the Springboks in Cape Town. Rennie’s side finished the game the stronger of the two sides, but trailed the whole 80 minutes at DHL Stadium, after the Springboks got off to a hot start.

The All Blacks struggled at lineout time, but improved the much-discussed scrum, which gained parity in the second Test. Speaking to former All Blacks halfback Justin Marshall, Rennie reflected on the contest.

Rugby.summary: The Kiwis showed flashes of the lethal execution that punished any South African indiscretion a week ago, but their own inaccuracies cost them time after time as the Springboks built a steady lead throughout the match.

New Zealand couldn’t recreate the magic of Ellis Park in Cape Town, threatening to mount a dramatic comeback late but ultimately running out of time at DHL Stadium. The Kiwis showed flashes of the lethal execution that punished any South African indiscretion a week ago, but their own inaccuracies cost them time after time as the Springboks built a steady lead throughout the match.

His subtle offload to Simon Parker resulted in a classy linebreak.

Rugby.title: Springboks hold firm against All Blacks fightback to level series
Rugby.summary: Not only did they lift their own performance, the Springboks forced Dave Rennie's side to make countless unforced errors, and make uncharacteristic kicks that handed possession back to the home side.
Rugby.body:
Staring down the barrel of trailing 2-0 in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks bounced back at DHL Stadium in Cape Town to level the four-Test series. The Springboks were always going to bite back fiercely, doing so in a way only the back-to-back Rugby World Cup winners could. The home side were dominant from the get-go, bursting out of the blocks to stun the All Blacks in the opening quarter. The visitors, who claimed a famous victory at Ellis Park in the first Test, struggled for large parts of the contest until the final 15 minutes, where Dave Rennie’s men battled back.

It was brutal by the Springboks. Not only did they lift their own performance, but the Springboks forced Dave Rennie’s side to make countless unforced errors and uncharacteristic kicks that handed possession back to the home side.

Rugby.title: Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series gets underway in Suzhou
Rugby.summary: The first leg of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series (ARESS 2026) is set to get underway this weekend.
Rugby.body:
The first leg of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series (ARESS 2026) is set to get underway this weekend, with the first of the two legs taking place in Suzhou, China. 12 teams for both the men’s and women’s tournaments are set to converge on the Jiangsu province city west of Shanghai for two days of action, with a combined log points across the two legs of action determining the outcome.

The second leg will take place in Colombo, Sri Lanka in October, with the two nations are the bottom of each respective table set to be relegated. The heavyweight sides to the men’s tournament are set to be hosts China, Hong Kong China and Japan, however several new additions are set to ask plenty of questions – with two newly promoted side in Kazakhstan and India.

Rugby.title: 'I am eternally grateful': Netherlands and Scotland A name squads for Amsterdam clash
Rugby.summary: Rugby Nederland will say goodbye to one of its greatest servants when its women's team take on a Scotland A in Amsterdam on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Rugby Nederland will say goodbye to one of its greatest servants when its women’s team take on a Scotland A in Amsterdam on Saturday. Dames XV head coach Gareth Gilbert will lead his team for a final time at home this weekend, before leading the team in Hong Kong China in WXV Global Series Challenger fixtures against Samoa, Brazil and Fiji.

At the conclusion of those three weeks, Gilbert will end his 15-year association with the Netherlands to take up a post as head coach of Pretoria Boys High School. Over the years, Gilbert has served as head coach of the Netherlands Men, Women’s Sevens and has also led the Men’s Under-20s since 2022. In he succeeded Sylke Haverkorn as head coach of the Dames XV. This year he led the team to a second-place finish in the Rugby Europe Championship.

Rugby.title: WRU posts pitch safety advice over hot, dry summer
Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union issues pitch safety advice for the new season after a record-breaking summer.
Rugby.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union has issued pitch safety advice to community clubs for the new season after a record-breaking summer. Wales recorded its hottest ever day on 24 June with temperatures soaring to 35.9C in Cardiff, while July was the driest since records began 190 years ago.

The weather has left rugby pitches across the country bone dry, with surfaces as hard as concrete. With the obvious injury risks to players, the WRU has written to all community clubs with guidance on how to assess the conditions before next week's opening matches.

Rugby.summary: Men's Rugby World Cup debutants Hong Kong China have decided to revert back to Andrew Douglas as head coach one year out from the tournament in Australia.
Rugby.body:
Men’s Rugby World Cup debutants Hong Kong China have decided to revert back to Andrew Douglas as head coach one year out from the tournament in Australia. Douglas, who successfully led the Asian team through RWC 2027 qualifying, stood down shortly after their ticket to Australia had been punched to focus on his Head of Technical Rugby role with the Hong Kong China RU.

Logan Asplin was promoted to the role of head coach in his place, having previously served as an assistant to Douglas, but the more experienced of the two Kiwis is now the man in charge again.

Rugby.title: Leicester sign Australian fly-half Bowen
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers sign Australian stand-off half Jack Bowen.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers have signed Australian fly-half Jack Bowen. Bowen, 22, has signed what Tigers call a "multi-year deal". He will spend the first year out of that on loan in Japan with the Tigers' partner club Mitsubishi Dynaboars.

The Kanagawa-based club are coached by former Nottingham and London Irish boss Glenn Delaney. "He'll come to Leicester via our partner club in Japan - Mitsubishi Dynaboars - to keep working on his game," said Tigers head coach Geoff Parling. "Then we look forward to seeing what he can do with us from 2027 onwards. Jack is someone who we think has some real potential."

Rugby.body:
New Zealand’s 33-16 win over South Africa in Johannesburg last weekend ended the Springboks’ hopes of beating their best-ever continuous run at the top of the World Rugby Men’s Rankings.

The Boks were just over halfway to matching their record 98-week unbroken reign, set between 2019-21, as they closed in on a whole year at No.1, but the defeat at Ellis Park demoted them to second place going into this weekend’s Cape Town rematch.

Rugby.body:
Munster could offer out-of-favour Gloucester fly-half Ross Byrne the chance to get his career back on track, with Jack Crowley set to be ruled out of action until the New Year.

Crowley hasn’t played since April with a lower limb vascular injury, and Munster announced earlier this week that he will miss at least the first half of the new season. Munster head coach Clayton McMillan is expected to ask if he can sign a replacement, and there are very few options available at this time of the season.

Rugby.summary: Incumbent Wallaroos Player of the Year, Tabua Tuinakauvadra, will make her return for Australia at WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Incumbent Wallaroos Player of the Year, Tabua Tuinakauvadra, will make her return for Australia at WXV Global Series. The 23-year-old back-row forward has not played a Test for the Wallaroos since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 as a result of separate knee injuries. During her time off the pitch, Tuinakauvadra missed the Pacific Four Series and the second Laurie O’Reilly Cup match in Auckland.

In addition to Tuinakauvadra, the Wallaroos Director of Women’s high performance, Tom Walsh, has also recalled Georgina Friedrichs and Faliki Pohiva. Tiarah Minns has also recovered from the neck injury that kept her out of Super Rugby Women’s action this season.

During her time off the pitch, Tuinakauvadra missed the Pacific Four Series and the second Laurie O’Reilly Cup match in Auckland.

In addition to Tuinakauvadra, the Wallaroos Director of Women’s high performance, Tom Walsh, has also recalled Georgina Friedrichs and Faliki Pohiva. Tiarah Minns has also recovered from the neck injury that kept her out of Super Rugby Women’s action this season.

Rugby.title: Bristol turn to Max Clark as stop-gap centre solution
Rugby.summary: Clark has been jobless since being part of the mass clearout of players by Newcastle at the end of last season.
Rugby.body:
Max Clark has been handed a PREM Rugby lifeline after being snapped up by Bristol Bears on a short-term deal. Clark has been jobless since being part of the mass clearout of players by Newcastle at the end of last season. But the Bears have now turned to the 30-year-old as their midfield resources are stretched with the start of the new season just around the corner.

The Welsh-born centre arrives at the Bears as cover for the club’s returning internationals during the first block of PREM Rugby Cup fixture. Benhard Janse van Rensburg, Tom Jordan and Matias Moroni are all unable to play until round one of the Gallagher PREM following their involvement for England, Scotland and Argentina over the summer.

Rugby.title: Jake White: How I'm sure Dave Rennie feels going into second Test
Rugby.summary: I have no doubt Dave Rennie will be feeling very confident about this Second Test.
Rugby.body:
I have no doubt Dave Rennie will be feeling very confident about this Second Test. Even with the Wallabies, who didn’t always prosper under his stewardship, the one team he fared well against was South Africa.

So he must be feeling pretty chipper right now. He hasn’t lost a game as All Blacks coach and he’s beaten Rassie in four out of their five games against each other. Which other coach has a better record against Rassie? I’m struggling to think of one.

Rugby.title: Springboks make two eve-of-match changes for second All Blacks Test
Rugby.summary: The Springboks have announced two changes to their starting XV for Test two of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series as a result of two injury updates.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks have announced two changes to their starting XV for Test two of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series as a result of two late injury updates. The first update sees Handre Pollard exit the matchday team after picking up what the team described as a “niggle” in a training session on Wednesday. The veteran’s withdrawal is covered by Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who steps into the No.10 jersey he wore last week. Meanwhile, on the bench, the No.23 jersey Feinberg-Mngomezulu was originally named in will now be given to Manie Libbok.

There is also a positive injury update from the South Africa camp, with Cheslin Kolbe declared fit for the Test. The superstar winger has been thrown straight into the starting team, taking Kurt-Lee Arendse’s place on the right wing. Arendse falls out of the matchday unit as a result.

Rugby.body:
While no doubt excited at the news that a new southern hemipshere fly-half has been snapped up by the club, Leicester fans will have to wait before seeing Jack Bowen in action.

Bowen has been signed from the NSW Waratahs on a multi-year deal but will arrive at Mattioli Woods Welford Road via a spell of club rugby in Japan. Leicester’s partner club, Mitsubishi Dynaboars, will get first use of the 22-year-old, who will spend the 2026-27 season gaining experience in Japan’s Rugby League One.

Rugby.title: Watch: Ex-NZ U20 playmaker's clever try as Hawke’s Bay stay unbeaten
Rugby.summary: Former New Zealand U20 playmaker Will Cole took the opportunity to start an NPC match at 10 with both hands.
Rugby.body:
Former New Zealand U20 playmaker Will Cole took the opportunity to start an NPC match at 10 with both hands, finishing with an 11-point haul as Hawke’s Bay maintained their unbeaten run with a 36-21 win away to Southland.

Cole made a series of appearances for New Zealand’s age-grad side at The Rugby Championship U20 in South Africa last May, before starting at first five-eighth in two of four matches at the World Rugby Junior World Championship in Georgia.

Rugby.title: USA Eagles hopeful goes first overall in 2026 MLR College Draft
Rugby.summary: With the first pick in the 2026 Major League Rugby College Draft, Old Glory DC have taken hard-working loose forward Logan Ballinger.
Rugby.body:
With the first pick in the 2026 Major League Rugby College Draft, Old Glory DC have taken hard-working loose forward Logan Ballinger, who was surrounded by Life University teammates when the news was announced on Thursday.

Ballinger is the latest MLR draftee to have come out of the prestigious collegiate rugby program, following in the footsteps of others like Conner Mooneyham, who holds a unique place in history as the competition’s first-ever draft choice.

Rugby.title: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii returns in rare role as Wallabies name team for Pumas
Rugby.summary: Suaalii missed the Flight Centre Series match against Japan in Townsville due to injury, but is back in the fold to face Los Pumas.
Rugby.body:
It’s been more than 645 days since Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii was last named on the bench for the Wallabies, but the 22-Test back will play that role this weekend when the Australians take on Argentina in San Salvador de Jujuy.

Suaalii missed the Flight Centre Series match against the Brave Blossoms in Townsville due to injury, but is back in the fold to face Los Pumas. 2025 John Eales Medal winner Len Ikitau has not been named in the matchday 23, with coach Les Kiss sticking with the most recent centre pairing.

Rugby.summary: Reports are surfacing that Springboks flyhalf Handre Pollard has been pulled from the second Test against the All Blacks in Cape Town.
Rugby.body:
Reports are surfacing that Springboks flyhalf Handre Pollard has been pulled from the second Test against the All Blacks in Cape Town. According to Netwerk24, the 32-year-old has a calf injury and will not take his place in the No.10 jersey.

Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu who started the first Test, was named on the bench with Pollard elevated into the starting line-up. Mannie Libbok is expected to replace Pollard but it is unclear yet who will start and who will be on the bench.

Rugby.summary: The maturity and resolve shown by Dave Rennie's team at Ellis Park bodes well for the Rugby World Cup crusade next year
Rugby.body:
It is maybe fitting that the All Blacks delivered their most resilient performance since the 2023 World Cup quarter-final defeat of Ireland at Ellis Park. Win a VIP match experience at the Baltimore Test, plus travel & accommodation up to $2,500.

Rugby.summary: The Wallabies need to win at least one of their two upcoming Tests in Argentina, but it will be no simple task.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have been in Argentina a few days now, getting ready for two Tests that will be both crucial for the ongoing evolution of the side under Les Kiss and also their biggest test under the new coach.

Los Pumas in Argentina remains among the toughest assignments in international rugby now. In the last two years alone, Argentina have claimed the scalps of New Zealand, South Africa, Australia and a French XV, as well as giving England an awful scare in the final game of the first block of Nations Championship matches in July.

Rugby.summary: Canada vice-captain Alexandra Tessier believes the national team have "hooked" home supporters with their Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 success.
Rugby.body:
Canada vice-captain Alexandra Tessier believes the national team have “hooked” home supporters with their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 success. This comes after Rugby Canada have confirmed that ticket sales for their BMO Field clash with England’s Red Roses have surpassed the attendance record for a standalone women’s rugby match in North America.

Taking place on Friday 16 October, Toronto’s BMO Field will see a repeat of the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final and start The Rugby Rematch Tour, presented by Canadian Tyre as part of WXV Global Series.

Rugby.title: Ospreys sign former Australia wing Koroibete
Rugby.summary: Ospreys add to their Australian contigent with the signing of former Wallabies wing Marika Koroibete.
Rugby.body:
Ospreys have made former Wallabies wing Marika Koroibete their fourth Australian signing of the summer. The 34-year-old will spend 2026-27 playing for the Swansea-based side in the United Rugby Championship (URC).

Koroibete, who won the last of his 63 Australia caps against New Zealand in September 2024, arrives after five seasons with Panasonic Wild Knights in Japan. "I'm really happy to be joining the Ospreys. I've heard some great things from the boys here already about the team and the environment, so I can't wait to get started," said Koroibete.

Rugby.title: Sophie de Goede retakes captaincy as Canada unveil squad for WXV
Rugby.summary: Reigning World Rugby Women's 15s Player of the Year, Sophie de Goede, has been reinstalled as captain of Canada.
Rugby.body:
Reigning World Rugby Women’s 15s Player of the Year, Sophie de Goede, has been reinstalled as captain of Canada ahead of the WXV Global Series. The 27-year-old goal-kicking forward has taken the captaincy back from Alexandra Tessier. Tessier took over the captaincy from De Goede after a long-term ACL injury kept her out of rugby for 13 months ahead of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

Upon her return to the pitch, De Goede was talismanic for Canada as they reached the Allianz Stadium final, where they lost 33-13 to England’s Red Roses in a repeat of the 2014 final.

Rugby.title: The recalled All Black who 'really suits' playing Springboks
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie has called on one of his biggest athletes to start against the Springboks in Cape Town this weekend after losing Josh Lord to injury.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has called on one of his most physical athletes to start against the Springboks in Cape Town this weekend after losing Josh Lord to an injury. The lock’s absence has triggered a reshuffle in the Kiwi pack, with Tupou Vaa’i moving from the blindside flank back to the second row, and Simon Parker coming into the starting loose forward trio.

Parker, who debuted for New Zealand during the 2025 Rugby Championship and is listed at 197 cm and 117 kg, has emerged as one of New Zealand’s most physical forwards in recent seasons and grabbed hold of the black No. 6 jersey under Scott Robertson’s watch last year.

Rugby.title: Aoibheann Reilly: 'Nothing can compare to pulling back on an Ireland jersey'
Rugby.summary: For the jersey presentations, a couple of days before Aoibheann Reilly's senior Ireland debut in 2022, Brian O’Driscoll dropped by to do the honours.
Rugby.body:
For the jersey presentations, a couple of days before Aoibheann Reilly’s senior Ireland debut in 2022, Brian O’Driscoll dropped by to do the honours. Almost 20 years after she had first posed for a picture with the Irish rugby legend, as a toddler, Reilly was positively beaming.

“It was kind of this full circle moment,” Reilly told RugbyPass. “Ireland were doing an open training session at Buccaneers (ahead of the 2003 World Cup), in Athlone. Their ground is only 20 minutes from our family house. My dad brought myself and my two brothers along. We got loads of pictures with the players, although I don’t look too pleased in any of them!

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie on All Blacks selection: 'The game on Tuesday made it a bit clearer'
Rugby.summary: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie hinted at changes for Test three of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour after announcing his matchday 23 for Test two.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie hinted at changes for Test three of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour after announcing his matchday 23 for Test two. The changes would be rewarding the players who lifted the All Blacks to victory over the Lions in a dramatic game at Ellis Park on Tuesday. It was a match in which New Zealand trailed for just shy of a full hour, but sprinted home with four consecutive tries in the final 30 minutes.

Some of the big statistical performers of the night included Ethan Blackadder with 15 carries, Rieko Ioane and Emoni Narawa with three linebreaks each, and Timoci Tavatavanawai with eight tackle busts.

Rugby.title: French rugby clubs handed massive cash windfall running to over 100 million
Rugby.summary: The Ligue Nationale de Rugby (LNR) has announced the distribution of €126.5m among the 30 clubs competing in the Top 14 and Pro D2 under its solidarity and investment redistribution mechanism.
Rugby.body:
The Ligue Nationale de Rugby (LNR) has announced the distribution of €126.5m among the 30 clubs competing in the Top 14 and Pro D2 under its solidarity and investment redistribution mechanism.

In its annual assessment, the LNR evaluated three metrics to determine the amount each club is entitled to receive: solidarity, sporting merit (season results and the number of players representing Les Bleus, and incentives (covering stadium conditions and the youth pathway).

Rugby.body:
Picture the scene: you’re helping your dad with a project in the garage. The smell of oil assaults your nostrils as Lynyrd Skynyrd crackles from a tinny radio. Without looking up, he asks you to fetch a tool from the toolbox. But which one?

A wrench? A screwdriver? Both are useful, and both can be used to tighten or loosen. But they are designed for different kinds of work: one gives you leverage, the other precision. Choose one and the entire operation changes.

Rugby.summary: South Africa tighthead prop Thomas du Toit is expecting the All Blacks' scrum to bounce back this week after enduring a tough afternoon against the Springboks at Ellis Park.
Rugby.body:
South Africa tighthead prop Thomas du Toit is expecting the All Blacks‘ scrum to bounce back this week after enduring a tough afternoon against the Springboks at Ellis Park in the first Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Though Dave Rennie’s side came away with the win in Johannesburg, their scrum was under immense pressure for the first hour of the match, with only the All Blacks’ substitute props able to stem the flow of penalties. Additionally, South Africa’s replacement props were not as destructive as Ox Nche and Wilco Louw had proven to be.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie addresses the Wellington warning looming large for All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Exactly how far the Springboks' tweaks can take them will be revealed on Saturday, but Rennie has some clear expectations.
Rugby.body:
The date is Saturday, September 13, 2025, and the All Blacks run out onto the Hnry Stadium turf to face the Springboks. Just seven days earlier, they’ve beaten their famous foes to extend their unbeaten Eden Park record. But this time, things are about to go very differently, and the ensuing 43-10 pummeling sets a record for the biggest defeat New Zealand has ever conceded. It’s a memory not so far from mind ahead of Saturday’s showdown at DHL Stadium.

Last weekend’s 33-16 win at Ellis Park has the Kiwis in the driver’s seat of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, affording them an opportunity to cement at least a drawn series with another win in Cape Town. The team can only find so much comfort in a singular win, though, with 2025’s Wellington warning looming large in camp.

Rugby.title: Loughborough name 'naturally competitive' coach as Emily Scarratt replacement
Rugby.summary: Nathan Smith has appointed a BUCS Super Rugby-winning head coach as the successor to Emily Scarratt in his coaching staff.
Rugby.body:
Nathan Smith has appointed a BUCS Super Rugby-winning head coach as the successor to Emily Scarratt in his coaching staff. Matt Campbell has taken the reins as assistant backs and attack coach after Scarratt left the East Midlands for a full-time assistant coach role with John Mitchell’s Red Roses side.

Over the past two years Campbell has led Loughborough University to the Women’s BUCS Super Rugby final, and ended the programme’s 21-year wait for a title in April with victory against Brunel University.

Rugby.summary: Munster announce that Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley is not expected to return from injury until the new year.
Rugby.body:

Having sat out Ireland's Nations Championship games against Australia, Japan and New Zealand last month, the 26-year-old will miss the competition's second block of games against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa in November.

Rugby.summary: Munster have confirmed that Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley is not expected to return to action until the new year as he continues his recovery from a lower-limb vascular injury.
Rugby.body:
Munster have confirmed that Ireland fly-half Jack Crowley is not expected to return to action until the new year as he continues his recovery from a lower-limb vascular injury.

The 26-year-old has been assessed by specialists, with medical advice ruling him out of the opening months of the 2026/27 campaign. Munster have stressed that ensuring Crowley makes a complete recovery remains the priority rather than accelerating his return.

Rugby.title: Harlequins snap up Zimbabwe winger Sigauke
Rugby.summary: Harlequins sign Zimbabwe's "real handful" of a winger Edward Sigauke, who will join the club next week.
Rugby.body:
Harlequins have signed Zimbabwe winger Edward Sigauke. The 22-year-old has played 12 times, scoring eight tries, for his country, having made his international debut in 2024. Quins head coach Jason Gilmore said: "Eddie is a player we've been tracking and we're really pleased to get his signing over the line.

"He's got tremendous speed and footwork that makes him a real handful for any defence, and we believe he's got all the raw tools to become a weapon for us out wide. "What excites us most is his potential - he's still developing as a player, and we can't wait to see how he grows within our environment as he takes the next steps in his career."

Rugby.title: Leicester Tigers report three-year fan high as confidence returns
Rugby.summary: Buoyed by an encouraging first season in charge under Geoff Parling, Leicester's season ticket sales for the 2026/27 campaign have topped five figures.
Rugby.body:
Buoyed by an encouraging first season in charge under Geoff Parling, Leicester’s season ticket sales for the 2026/27 campaign have topped five figures. Just over a fortnight out from the first competitive home fixture of the season against Newcastle in the PREM Rugby Cup, the Tigers have reported their highest sales for three years. So far, Leicester have sold 10,400 season tickets, which start at £199 for adults and £50 for U18s.

Leicester won the Cup in March and reached the PREM play-offs after a strong second half to the league season, only to lose to East Midlands rivals Northampton in the semi-finals.

The 2026 FISU World University Championship Rugby Sevens takes place from September 4 to 6 in Stellenbosch , South Africa. Rugby.title: PWR attendances rise by 23% after World Cup
Rugby.summary: Premiership Women's Rugby says average attendances rose by 23.4% during the 2025-26 season, which concluded in June with Saracens winning a record fourth title.
Rugby.body:
Premiership Women's Rugby says average attendances rose by 23.4% during the 2025-26 season, which concluded in June with Saracens winning a record fourth title. The numbers have been aided by the boost the sport received by England winning a home World Cup at Twickenham in September 2025 and come despite the departure of United States star Ilona Maher from Bristol Bears.

Maher, who is the most followed rugby union player in the world on social media, generated unprecedented attention for the league during her stint in Bristol during the 2024-25 campaign.

Rugby.title: France prop Jefferson Poirot confirms injury amid strange career admission
Rugby.summary: France and Bordeaux-Begles loosehead Jefferson Poirot will miss the start of the season after spraining his knee, French outlet RMC have confirmed.
Rugby.body:
France and Bordeaux-Begles loosehead Jefferson Poirot will miss the start of the season after spraining his knee, French outlet RMC have confirmed. The 33-year-old, who came out of international retirement in July to represent Les Bleus for the first time since 2020, will miss the next six to eight weeks with the injury, Bordeaux head coach Yannick Bru has confirmed.

The injury will leave the loosehead in a fitness race to make the beginning of Bordeaux’s Investec Champions Cup title defence, which begins with a round one trip to Gloucester on October 16.

Rugby.title: Telling stat underlines Springboks' glaring Achilles heel against All Blacks
Rugby.summary: After an unconvincing 17-10 win against Argentina and last weekend's 33-16 loss to New Zealand, South Africa have mustered just 33 points from their last two fixtures.
Rugby.body:
A combination of brilliant defence by the All Blacks and butchered attacking opportunities nullified the Springboks’ ability to turn territorial pressure into points at Ellis Park last weekend, resulting in their 33-16 loss.

Following on from an unconvincing 17-10 win against Argentina, over the last two games South Africa have mustered just 33 points, their joint-lowest total in back-to-back Tests since the very early days of Rassie Erasmus’ reign in 2018.

Rugby.title: The end is in sight as Louis Bielle-Biarrey plots his future
Rugby.summary: French superstar winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey is closing in on a two-year contract extension with Bordeaux-Bègles that will keep him at the club until the summer of 2029.
Rugby.body:
French superstar winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey is closing in on a two-year contract extension with Bordeaux-Bègles that will keep him at the club until the summer of 2029. Bielle-Biarrey, 23, has scored 29 tries in 27 appearances for Les Bleus and been named Player of the Tournament in each of the last two Six Nations after helping France secure back-to-back titles.

He entered the final year of his current agreement in July and has been in talks with Bordeaux president Laurent Marti for weeks in a bid to reach a new agreement. Although he wasn’t likely to leave, minor details, including his Adidas deal, have taken time to iron out. The latest reports from France suggest the end is now in sight.

Rugby.summary: Wales superstar Louis Rees-Zammit has issued an ominous warning and put the Gallagher PREM on notice that he has settled back into rugby at Bristol Bears and is ready for a big season.
Rugby.body:
Wales superstar Louis Rees-Zammit has issued an ominous warning and put the Gallagher PREM on notice that he has settled back into rugby at Bristol Bears and is ready for a big season.

Rees-Zammit, 25, joined the Bears last July after spending 18 months in the NFL with the Kansas City Chiefs and the Jacksonville Jaguars, scoring seven tries in 13 games despite injuries and flitting between the wing and full-back.

Rugby.title: Gallagher PREM 2026/27 squads rated: Bath
Rugby.summary: Johann van Graan begins his fifth term of office at The Rec without two of the standout performers of his reign in charge - Thomas du Toit and Alfie Barbeary.
Rugby.body:
Compared to the past two seasons, which resulted in a first league trophy in 29 years and a title defence that fell just short, Bath supporters’ confidence is not as high as it once was entering the new campaign, despite the bookies marking them down as marginal favourites ahead of reigning champions Northampton.

Johann van Graan begins his fifth term of office at The Rec without two standout performers – Thomas du Toit and Alfie Barbeary – and with a new attack coach, albeit someone very familiar to both him and chief playmaker, Finn Russell, in ex-Munster man Mike Prendergast.

Rugby.title: 'South Africa have the All Blacks right where they want them'
Rugby.summary: The Springboks lost the first Test convincingly, but adversity seems to compel Rassie Erasmus' world champions to greater heights.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have made a terrible mistake. They have beaten the Springboks. Win a VIP match experience at the Baltimore Test, plus travel & accommodation up to $2,500. Worse, they have beaten them convincingly enough to ensure every South African player, coach and supporter will spend every minute until Saturday’s kick-off thinking about little else. The score was 33-16. New Zealand scored five tries to South Africa’s one. The Boks lost their world number one ranking, their 12-match winning streak and the first Test of a four-match series.

In other words, Rassie Erasmus and his players are exactly where they want to be. The Springboks are at their most dangerous when they are unhappy. They need to feel aggrieved. They need a problem. They need to believe the outside world has reached a premature conclusion about them. The All Blacks have just provided all three.

Rugby.title: 'We felt the pressure': Cobus Reinach flags All Blacks tactics
Rugby.summary: South Africa scrum-half Cobus Reinach has admitted that his side "felt the pressure" the All Blacks exerted as they fell 33-16 in the first Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
South Africa scrum-half Cobus Reinach has admitted that his side “felt the pressure” the All Blacks exerted as they fell 33-16 in the first Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

The veteran scrum-half, who will start this week in Cape Town after coming on from the bench at Ellis Park, spoke specifically about the way Dave Rennie’s side attacked the breakdown, with both Reinach and Grant Williams, whom he replaced, harassed by the All Blacks forwards all match.

Rugby.title: 'Nothing comes close to this place': Freddie Burns returns to Leicester
Rugby.summary: The former England fly-half is back at the club where he had two spells as a player after being appointed as the Tigers' kicking coach.
Rugby.body:
Former England fly-half Freddie Burns has returned to Leicester, where he had two spells as a player, after being appointed as the club’s kicking coach. Leicester’s 2022 PREM-winning hero hung up his boots at the end of last season, having seen out his career in Romania, and has been given a full-time contract.

He is the second former Tigers player to join the coaching team in the space of just over a week, after Craig Newby was brought on board as the club’s part-time forwards skills coach.

Rugby.title: National 7s Circuit: Kabras Sugar narrows lead on KCB
Rugby.summary: The National 7s Circuit in Kenya is set for an electric final fortnight of action in September.
Rugby.body:
The National 7s Circuit in Kenya is set for an electric final fortnight of action in September, the injection of guest side Emerging Uganda and Kabras Sugar proving formidable challengers to defending champions KCB.

The tournament crossed the halfway mark at the Driftwood 7s in Mombasa last week, with KCB unable to defend their 2025 title, going down 15-5 to Kabras Sugar in the final thanks to a player-of-the-final performance from sevens star Kevin Wekesa.

Rugby.summary: Triston Reilly has played in the NRL for the Wests Tigers, the Australia Men’s Sevens side and most recently for the NSW Waratahs.
Rugby.body:
Triston Reilly played a few NRL games for the Wests Tigers, represented the Australia Men’s Sevens side and spent multiple seasons with the NSW Waratahs, but a conversation with Stephen Larkham convinced the winger to move to Australia’s capital.

The ACT Brumbies announced on July 15 that Reilly has inked a two-year deal. Reilly played 40 matches for the Waratahs but will now wear a different club’s colours in Super Rugby Pacific next year, but will first suit up for the Brums in Super Rugby AUS.

Rugby.title: Tom Hooper explains why injury setback became a ‘blessing in disguise’
Rugby.summary: Wallabies backrower Tom Hooper played 24 games for club and country last season before linking up with the Exeter Chiefs.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies backrower Tom Hooper played 24 games for club and country last season before linking up with the Exeter Chiefs, going on to make more than 20 appearances. ‘Hoops’ returned to the Wallabies fold in July, but then injury struck – only it proved to be “a blessing in disguise.”

Hooper made a 12-minute cameo off the bench in a 33-31 defeat to Ireland in Sydney, but the loose forward would take no further part in the July Tests. The Wallabies confirmed the following week that Hooper had picked up a shoulder injury.

Rugby.title: The unjustified vilification of Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu
Rugby.summary: Since returning as the Boks flyhalf against Argentina, he's had two performances that are below his game-breaking standard from 2025.
Rugby.body:
When Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu came off with an ankle injury in the act of scoring a try for the Stormers in their URC quarter-final in late May, it seemed his international season was potentially over.

SA Rugby mag reported a three-to-six-month recovery timeline for a syndesmosis injury. After surgery in June, the No.10 was back playing in just 10 weeks. From three months down to two and a half, ahead of the biggest series of his career.

Rugby.title: Tim Walsh on the ‘bright’ Wallaroos future, impact of sevens stars
Rugby.summary: While the result overall was a disappointing one, the match did come with small glimmers of promise.
Rugby.body:
The 100th test match for the Wallaroos proved a frustrating one for Rugby Australia’s Director of Women’s High Performance Tim Walsh and his new coaching team, the Black Ferns running out 66-19 and handing the women in gold their second heaviest defeat ever.

However, speaking after the match, the result has made Walsh all the more determined to get the XVs stars into a full time, high performance environment, buoyed by the success and competitiveness of the sevens stars injected into the side.

Rugby.summary: South African-born Japan centre Dylan Riley had already faced the Wallabies three times before taking the field in Townsville on August 15.
Rugby.body:
South African-born Japan centre Dylan Riley had already faced the Wallabies three times before taking the field in Townsville on August 15. The former Australia U20s back trekked a unique rugby path which led to that Test, but Riley “wouldn’t change it for anything.”

Harry Hockings was selected in the same Australia squad for the 2017 World Rugby Junior World Championship in Georgia, but those two were draped in red and white earlier this month, both scoring one try each against some of their age-grade teammates.

Rugby.summary: It was a night of linebreaks and freestyle rugby at Ellis Park on Tuesday, with the All Blacks completing a wild comeback against a Lions team that outperformed expectations in front of a vocal Johannesburg crowd.
Rugby.body:
It was a night of linebreaks and freestyle rugby at Ellis Park on Tuesday, with the All Blacks completing a wild comeback against a Lions team that outperformed expectations in front of a vocal Johannesburg crowd.

Starring in the performance was powerful All Blacks midfielder Timoci Tavatavanawai, who led the game with eight tackle busts on 13 carries, while making three linebreaks, running for 137 metres with the ball in hand, winning two steals, and making four offloads.

Rugby.title: 'Grit and guts': Rieko Ioane on scratchy All Blacks victory over Lions
Rugby.summary: "This is my third time playing this Lions team, and I sort of knew coming into this game that they were probably the least affected by in terms of international selection.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks outside-back Rieko Ioane has reflected on what was a patchy team performance against the Lions at Ellis Park in Johannesburg. The All Blacks’ last midweek clash didn’t go exactly to plan, but Ioane and other experienced players helped Dave Rennie’s side overcome a powerful Lions team at their home stadium.

The Kiwis needed impact from Xavier Numia, Bradley Slater, Saula Ma’u, and Jamie Hannah to secure the midweek victory, after a slow start by Rennie’s men. The Blues midfielder crossed twice during the second-half comeback by the All Blacks, picking off an intercept in the 55th minute. His first of the evening was from a Beauden Barrett tip-on pass, putting Ioane through a huge gap in the Lions’ defence.

Rugby.body:

The Blues loose-forward was named on the bench for last weekend’s clash against the Springboks, but was replaced by Chiefs No.6 Simon Parker on gameday. Rennie confirmed the news in his post-match press conference in Johannesburg, after the All Blacks’ 41-35 victory over the Lions.

Rugby.title: Burns returns to Tigers in coaching role
Rugby.summary: Former England and Leicester Tigers fly-half Freddie Burns returns to the Prem club as kicking coach.
Rugby.body:
Former England and Leicester Tigers fly-half Freddie Burns has returned to the Prem club as kicking coach. The 36-year-old landed one of the most famous kicks in the club's history when he slotted a last-minute drop-goal against Saracens to seal Tigers' 2022 Premiership title victory at Twickenham.

Burns' move into coaching with his former club comes just three weeks after he announced his retirement as a professional player. The playmaker, who was capped five times for England between 2012 and 2014, had two spells with Tigers in an eclectic career in which he also featured for Gloucester and Bath, as well as sides in New Zealand and Japan before seeing out his career as a player-coach in Romania with Dinamo Bucuresti.

Rugby.title: Canada's Pacific Nations Cup squad missing experienced French-based trio
Rugby.summary: Head coach Steve Meehan has named five uncapped players in Jamie Armstrong, Bryce Worden, Sam Turner, Ryan Cozens and Jack Gore, the Candian University Rookie of the Year in 2025.
Rugby.body:
Canada’s squad for the upcoming September Test window is missing three experienced players – hooker Andrew Quattrin, lock Evan Olmstead and No.8 Tyler Ardron. The trio, who boast 109 caps between them, are unavailable for selection for the trip to Japan, which involves a one-off fixture against the Brave Blossoms followed by two games in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup, because of their club commitments in France.

Ardron and Olmstead are at the beginning of new careers with Provence and Nice, with the Pro D2 season only a couple of days away, while Quattrin’s season with Nationale outfit Carcassonne, who he joined from Valence, is already up and running.

Rugby.title: All Blacks' latest injury replacement withdrawn from Lions game with illness
Rugby.summary: Ofa Tu'ungafasi's All Blacks return has hit a snag, with the veteran prop coming down with an illness quickly after landing in South Africa.
Rugby.body:
Ofa Tu’ungafasi’s All Blacks return has hit a snag, with the veteran prop coming down with an illness quickly after landing in South Africa. The 34-year-old only arrived in the country on Monday morning, getting a late call-up after Ethan de Groot suffered a concussion in Saturday’s 33-16 win over the Springboks. He was immediately named by Dave Rennie in the No.17 jersey in Tuesday evening’s match against the Lions. His withdrawal means Xavier Numia will come onto the All Blacks’ bench.

Tu’ungafasi hasn’t been seen in black since 2024’s northern tour, before a neck injury derailed his 2025. With the change, New Zealand’s reserve front row loses 66 Tests of experience.

Tennis.title: GB's Fery returns to Grand Slam stage
Tennis.summary: Shock Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery returns to the Grand Slam stage when he faces Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
As the top stars congregated in New York for last year's US Open, Arthur Fery was looking in from the outside. The Briton had just crept back inside the world's top 300 after winning an ATP Challenger event in Colombia and admits it was a "bit painful" watching players at the pinnacle of the sport.

Twelve months on, the 24-year-old is rubbing shoulders with the elite at Flushing Meadows, thanks to the stunning run to the Wimbledon semi-finals which has likely changed his life forever.

Tennis.title: A loss that feels different
Tennis.summary: After Novak Djokovic's latest bid for a historic 25th major title ends in tears in New York, where does the most decorated men's player of the Open era go from here?
Tennis.body:
Be warned: Novak Djokovic has made a fool of those who have doubted him before. Some questioned if the Serb would challenge for the sport's top honours again after he dropped out of the world's top 20 amid a two-year major title drought in 2018.

Djokovic proceeded to win four of the following five Grand Slams, doubling his tally of majors with 12 across the next six years. But three years have now passed since he landed his men's record 24th major title at the US Open.

Tennis.title: Wawrinka feels the love on Grand Slam goodbye
Tennis.summary: Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka is given an emotional send-off at the US Open following the final Grand Slam match of his career.
Tennis.body:
Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka felt the love at the US Open after being given an emotional send-off following the final Grand Slam match of his career. The 41-year-old Swiss is retiring at the end of the season and looked close to tears as he received a rapturous reception after a straight-set defeat by Italy's Matteo Berrettini.

Wawrinka, who won the US Open in 2016, was initially overlooked by tournament organisers for a wildcard, but was given a last-minute reprieve following American recipient Patrick Kypson's withdrawal.

Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open. Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed from defending his title from last year.

After a 139-day wait, Carlos Alcaraz is back to winning ways on the singles court. The seven-time major winner walked on to Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday to begin his US Open title defence after spending just over four months on the sidelines with a wrist injury.

And he delighted fans with his entertaining brand of tennis and infectious energy as he beat Russia's Roman Safiullin 6-4 6-4 6-4. Alcaraz was forced to watch from the sidelines as rivals Alexander Zverev and Jannik Sinner lifted the French Open and Wimbledon titles this summer.

Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka blocks out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka blocked out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat". The two-time defending champion has suffered a dip in form in recent months after a stellar start to the season in which she reached the Australian Open final and completed the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami.

Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under serious threat and she risks ending the year without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022. However, she avoided an early slip-up as she held off a resilient Osorio to win 6-2 6-4 on her return to Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Tennis.title: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York?
Tennis.summary: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina. Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.

Tennis.title: Midnight matches and money disputes
Tennis.summary: BBC Sport explores the ongoing dispute over scheduling issues and late-night finishes at tennis' Grand Slam events.
Tennis.body:
When Venus Williams was awarded a wildcard for the women's singles at the US Open, she was chosen for a primetime match slot in the first round - Sunday night, on Arthur Ashe, against compatriot Sofia Kenin in front of a home crowd for possibly the final time as a solo player.

But Williams and Kenin did not end up playing on Sunday. Instead they stepped on to court just after midnight on Monday, with Kenin completing a win in straight sets shortly after the clock struck 2am local time in New York.

Tennis.title: From playing Serena Williams on screen to following in her footsteps
Tennis.summary: Having played a young Serena Williams on the big screen, teenager Thea Frodin is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
Thea Frodin once played a young Serena Williams on the big screen. Now, the teenager is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open. Five years ago, Frodin was chosen as a tennis-playing body double for the actress cast as her childhood idol in the Oscar-nominated film 'King Richard'.

That involved the then 12-year-old American working alongside actor Will Smith as he portrayed Richard Williams, the father of sisters Serena and Venus. "Being able to play the role of somebody that I looked up to for my whole life was super special," Frodin told the WTA website., external

Five years ago, Frodin was chosen as a tennis-playing body double for the actress cast as her childhood idol in the Oscar-nominated film 'King Richard'.

That involved the then 12-year-old American working alongside actor Will Smith as he portrayed Richard Williams, the father of sisters Serena and Venus. "Being able to play the role of somebody that I looked up to for my whole life was super special," Frodin told the WTA website., external

Tennis.title: US Open: Novak Djokovic loses to Mariano Navone in longest first round match of his career in Grand Slams
Tennis.summary: US Open: Novak Djokovic loses to Mariano Navone in longest first round match of his career in Grand Slams Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic fell at the first hurdle as his tilt at a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam came to a shocking end to Argentine Mariano Navone in a five-set marathon at the US Open.

The 39-year-old went down 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 to the world No 49 in a match that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. It was the longest opening match of a Grand Slam in Djokovic's career and the earliest exit at a major since the 2006 Australian Open.

Tennis.title: Djokovic in tears during US Open first-round exit
Tennis.summary: An emotional Novak Djokovic suffers a US Open first-round defeat which provides further evidence that age is catching up with the 39-year-old great.
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic broke down in tears during a US Open first-round defeat by Argentina's Mariano Navone which provided further evidence age is fast catching up with the 39-year-old great.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was overcome by emotion in the deciding set of a dramatic match where he struggled physically throughout and had to vomit into a towel bin. Djokovic, seeded fourth, showed the fight for which he has always been renowned before succumbing to a 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 loss in a humid New York.

Tennis.title: GB's Samuel earns first win at a Grand Slam
Tennis.summary: British qualifier Toby Samuel breaks more new ground with a dominant victory over Tomas Machac on his US Open debut.
Tennis.body:
British qualifier Toby Samuel broke more new ground with a dominant victory over Tomas Machac on his US Open main-draw debut. The 23-year-old came from a set down in each of his three qualifying matches in New York this week to guarantee a third Grand Slam appearance of the year.

However, he had no such issues against former world number 20 Machac, wrapping up a 6-2 6-3 6-2 victory in just over 90 minutes to register his first win at a Grand Slam. "It means everything to me. It's what I dreamt of as a kid watching these big tournaments," Samuel told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Tennis.title: Tearful Federer inducted into Hall of Fame
Tennis.summary: Roger Federer says being inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame is "one of the greatest honours" of his life.
Tennis.body:
Roger Federer has been inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, describing the moment as "one of the greatest honours" of his life. The 20-time Grand Slam singles champion, who retired in 2022, was tearful at the ceremony in Newport, Rhode Island, as he reflected on his glittering career in front of tennis greats including Billie Jean King and John McEnroe.

After make his debut in 1998 at the age of 16, Federer won a men's-record eight Wimbledon titles, six Australian Open crowns, five US Opens and one French Open. "This is one of the greatest honours of my life," Federer, 45, said.

Tennis.summary: Arthur Fery misses out on his first ATP Tour title with a straight-set defeat by Ignacio Buse in the final of the Winston-Salem Open.
Tennis.body:
Arthur Fery missed out on his first ATP Tour title with a straight-set defeat by Ignacio Buse in the final of the Winston-Salem Open. Fery, who was the talk of Wimbledon as he reached the semi-finals of his home major in July, lost 6-3 6-2 to Peru's Buse.

The 24-year-old was the first Briton to reach the final of the ATP 250 tournament in North Carolina and will rise to 33 in the world rankings as a result - overtaking Cameron Norrie as British number one.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu won the US Open five years ago. Can she ever return to those heights?
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu won the US Open five years ago. Can she ever return to those heights? The Herald
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu winning the US Open feels like both a recent memory, and like it happened a lifetime ago. The 2026 US Open begins in New York today and marks five years since the young Brit made that remarkable run to the title at Flushing Meadows.

So much has happened since Raducanu made all different types of history in 2021, though, and the past five years have panned out in a way few would have predicted as she held the trophy aloft - for all the wrong reasons.
