Tennis.title: Fighting to stay No 1
Tennis.summary: Will Aryna Sabalenka rediscover her mojo? How will Carlos Alcaraz's comeback go? And can Novak Djokovic win? It's time for the 2026 US Open singles.
Tennis.body:
All was bright in Aryna Sabalenka's world when she completed a rare 'Sunshine Double' earlier this season. Becoming only the fifth woman to win the Indian Wells and Miami titles back-to-back, Sabalenka emphasised her position as the dominant player on the WTA Tour and created a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings.

But a difficult period quickly followed - seemingly out of nowhere - leaving the 28-year-old Belarusian clinging on to her position going into the US Open, which starts on Sunday.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper x Axel Arigato Reveal 'Midnight' Sneakers Collaboration
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper x Axel Arigato Reveal 'Midnight' Sneakers Collaboration Yahoo
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper and Axel Arigato have unveiled "Midnight," the final chapter in their trilogy of sneaker collaborations. Ahead of the US Open, the UK tennis star is completing the trilogy of collaborations with "Midnight," a black take on the Dice silhouette with teal accents. Following "Dusk" and "Rise," the new pair of sneakers celebrates the institution of night sessions. The timing of its release, on Wednesday (Aug. 26), coincides with the start of the US Open, which became the first Grand Slam to play under floodlights in 1975.

"Everything about New York feels bigger at night," said Jack Draper of the final sneaker collaboration in the trilogy. "The city, the noise, those late sessions—it's got that Gotham energy I've always loved. Midnight is the shoe for that: dark, sharp, made for after hours. It felt like the only way to finish the trilogy."

British tennis stars Emma Raducanu and Jack Draper have withdrawn from the final tennis grand slam of the year -- the US Open. Raducanu famously rose to fame after winning the event in 2021 at just 18 years-old. She worked her way through the qualifying rounds and then went on to win 10 straight matches without dropping a single set.

Draper reached the semifinals at Flushing Meadows in 2024, but his bid to go deeper into the tournament this year has now been stalled again. Both stars have the potential to be a success, but their injuries have proved to be major setbacks in reaching the top.

Tennis.title: Injury uncertainty led to 'intrusive thoughts' for Alcaraz
Tennis.summary: Seven-time major champion Carlos Alcaraz says not knowing when he would be able to return from a wrist injury was most challenging part of his long absence.
Tennis.body:
Seven-time major champion Carlos Alcaraz says dealing with "intrusive thoughts" over when he would be able to return from his wrist injury was the most challenging part of his long absence.

Spain's Alcaraz, 23, has not played a singles match since mid-April but says he feels "great" as he prepares to make his comeback at the US Open, which begins in New York on Sunday.

Tennis.title: 'I learned from Murray'
Tennis.summary: Andy Murray has long been a guiding figure for British tennis, but newly-married Katie Boulter will not be following his lead when it comes to keeping her wedding ring safe as she prepares for the US Open.
Tennis.body:
Andy Murray has long been a guiding figure for British tennis, but newly-married Katie Boulter will not be following his lead when it comes to keeping her wedding ring safe. Three-time Grand Slam champion Murray, who married wife Kim in 2015, famously briefly lost his wedding band after playing with it tied to his shoe laces.

Murray had left his trainers - with the ring still attached - under a car to dry out after a practice session in California in 2021, and after discovering they were missing the next day, was eventually reunited with both after putting out an appeal for their return.

Tennis.body:

Alcaraz's long absence has clouded his prospects, but the seven-time Grand Slam champion has built a reputation for producing his best tennis on the grandest stages and cannot be discounted despite the uncertainty surrounding his return.

Tennis.title: Why is Emma Raducanu not playing at the 2026 US Open?
Tennis.summary: Why is Emma Raducanu not playing at the 2026 US Open? bolavip.com
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu will miss the 2026 US Open after a stress fracture in her right lower leg forced her out of the tournament. The former champion had already been sidelined since Wimbledon, and her latest setback leaves her absent from the Grand Slam she famously won in 2021.

The timing is particularly frustrating for her, who had started to rebuild momentum earlier this season. She reached the final at Queen’s Club in June, her second WTA final of the year, before the leg problem worsened.

Tennis.title: US Open Tennis: News, draw, schedule, results and updates from Flushing Meadows in New York
Tennis.summary: US Open Tennis: News, draw, schedule, results and updates from Flushing Meadows in New York Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Jacob Fearnley and veteran Heather Watson were among the six British winners at US Open qualifying in New York. Fearnley advanced to the third and final qualifying round with a hard-fought 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-4 victory over Frenchman Luka Pavlovic that lasted two hours and 18 minutes.

The 25-year-old Scot appeared to be coasting when 4-2 ahead in the second set, but Pavlovic broke back and then won the tie break after saving a match point at 5-4. Fearnley, however, kept his composure to break at 3-2 in the deciding set, then saved three break points in the final game before closing out victory.

Tennis.title: Fery beats Kovacevic to reach Winston-Salem semi-final
Tennis.summary: Britain's Arthur Fery comes from a set down to beat Aleksandar Kovacevic and book his place in the semi-finals of the Winston-Salem Open.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Arthur Fery came from a set down to beat Aleksandar Kovacevic and book his place in the semi-finals of the Winston-Salem Open. Fourth seed Fery, who won five games in a row from 5-5 in the second set, claimed a 3-6 7-5 6-3 victory in Thursday's last-eight match in North Carolina.

After breaking Kovacevic to take the second set, Fery opened up a 3-0 lead in the third, serving out to clinch his first semi-final appearance since Wimbledon in July. The 24-year-old will face James Duckworth, who he beat in Cincinnati earlier this month, in the last four, after the Australian defeated Hungarian 15th seed Fabian Marozsan 6-7 (4-7) 6-2 6-4.

Tennis.title: 'A generational icon'
Tennis.summary: Venus Williams has not won a singles match in over a year but has received numerous wildcards to compete. The reasons why go beyond just tennis.
Tennis.body:
Venus Williams has broken many acres of new ground as a tennis player, with five Wimbledon singles titles among her multiple achievements. The 46-year-old has been playing professionally for nearly 30 years, but her last 14 singles matches have all ended in defeat.

With a world ranking of 611, Williams is reliant on wildcards to compete. She has had 11 already this season - and the United States Tennis Association (USTA) has offered her a 12th so she can play at the US Open, where she will face fellow Grand Slam champion Sofia Kenin in the first round.

Tennis.title: Alcaraz draws Safiullin at US Open, tough start for Fery
Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz starts his US Open title defence against Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first serious examination of his fitness following a long-term wrist injury.
Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz will start his US Open title defence against Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first serious examination of his fitness following a long-term wrist injury. Alcaraz, who won the men's title in New York last year, has not played a competitive singles match for more than four months because of inflammation in his playing right wrist.

The 23-year-old Spaniard missed this season's French Open and Wimbledon as a result of the issue, which did not require surgery, before making his return to court in the US Open mixed doubles alongside Serena Williams earlier this week.

Tennis.title: Mensik & Muchova win US Open mixed doubles title
Tennis.summary: Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik save two match points on their way to the US Open mixed doubles title and $1m in prize money.
Tennis.body:
Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik saved two match points on their way to the US Open mixed doubles title and $1m in prize money. Mensik hit a 131mph ace on a third championship point to seal a 6-3 1-6 10-6 win in the final against Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.

That victory came after they saved match points in their semi-final against Andrey Rublev and Mirra Andreeva. It is a first Grand Slam title for both players and comes just over six weeks after Muchova was beaten by compatriot Linda Noskova in the Wimbledon final.

Tennis.title: Serena and Venus Williams given wild card to compete in 2026 US Open women's doubles tournament
Tennis.summary: Serena and Venus Williams given wild card to compete in 2026 US Open women's doubles tournament Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Serena and Venus Williams will play together in the 2026 US Open women's doubles after being given a wild card to enter the tournament. The sisters played competitively together for the first time since the 2022 US Open at the Cincinnati Open earlier this month, and will now return to Grand Slam action at the scene of their last major outing as a pair.

Serena made a sensational return to tennis during the grass-court season after almost four years out of the professional game, but the 44-year-old suffered a knee injury during a first-round singles loss at Wimbledon which led to her and Venus withdrawing from the doubles at the All England Club.

Tennis.body:
Jack Draper is officially no longer participating in the Grand Slam tournament starting next week. This makes him one of 17 players (so far) that have dropped out of the 2026 US Open, including most recently Jannik Sinner and Holger Rune.

The reason for Draper’s absence is a bone bruise in his left arm, which he has continued to battle over the last few months. This injury is especially troubling for the 24-year-old since his left arm is his dominant one. He will take more time to recover and hopefully return to competitive play soon.

Tennis.body:
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to. That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.

Tennis.body:
Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York. The 41-year-old will retire at the end of year and was given a wildcard for this year's Australian Open and Wimbledon, while reaching the French Open main-draw on ranking.

He reached the third round in Melbourne and lost a pair of entertaining first-round matches in Paris and Wimbledon respectively. The US Open has received some criticism for its decision not to award a wildcard to 2016 champion Wawrinka, who did not enter qualifying despite being inside the cut-off.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: If the group ahead is slow, can I take more than 3 minutes to find my ball?
Golf.summary: If you're waiting on the group ahead, can you use the extra time to search for your ball for more than 3 minutes? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: If the group ahead is slow, can I take more than 3 minutes to find my ball? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Let’s say, while playing behind a slow group, I hit my ball into an area where I can’t find it in the allotted 3 minutes. If I couldn’t play my next shot anyway because they’re delaying my pace of play, can I continue to look for my ball without penalty? – Barry Nygard, via email

It’s a reasonable thought, Barry…but reasonableness isn’t the standard here. The three-minute search time is a hard deadline, regardless of whether slowpokes would have had you waiting. Once you or your caddie (or your partner or partner’s caddie in partner formats) start to search for your ball, if it’s not found within that allotted three minutes it is lost and no longer in play, and Rule 18.2b requires that you play under stroke and distance. (See also Definition of Lost.)

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's Tour Championship near-miss leads him to great 'philosophical question'
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland had the Tour Championship in his grasp before Scottie Scheffler grabbed it. That near-miss has Hovland facing a big question. The post Viktor Hovland’s Tour Championship near-miss leads him to great ‘philosophical question’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Viktor Hovland is both a big-picture thinker and someone who is myopically focused. Such is the blessing and curse of the gifted, those given rare talent and a brain that never stops tinkering.

So after watching Scottie Scheffler run past him on Sunday at the Tour Championship, Hovland looked at the 10,000-foot view of his season, one that saw him beat Scheffler in a playoff at the Travelers and hold the 54-hole lead at East Lake. It was a season in which he contended while still searching for the feeling that has been missing since he started re-working his swing after his 2023 FedEx Cup win. Viktor Hovland is still searching for Viktor Hovland. So, in that sense, it’s positive that he can still contend with and beat the best in the world while trying to reach through smoke to grab whom he used to be. But the other part of Hovland, the one who is focused on the small details of everything, saw himself lose the first 54-hole lead of his career because he’s still not that Viktor Hovland.

Golf.title: This common swing fault could make you a better putter
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tommy O'Brien Jr. shares how thinking about a "hook" could help you become a better putter. The post This common swing fault could make you a better putter appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Hitting better putts can be easily achieved through understanding what type of full-swing motion makes a ball roll better. Every golfer has hit a hook or a slice with their full swing, but which one makes the ball roll out more? We all know the answer: the hook. Many of the top putters throughout history illustrate this well, as almost all of them have fought a hook with their full swing at some point in their careers.

In my experience, it’s uncanny how often players employ traits of their full swing in their putting stroke. Think about the players who have struggled with putting throughout their careers. Typically, they are some of the best ball strikers in the world — players who hit a “trap cut,” allowing them to dominate the ball-striking categories while falling short on the greens.

Golf.title: 5 winners (besides Scottie Scheffler) from PGA Tour's playoffs
Golf.summary: By traditional measurements (lowest score, most victories) Scottie Scheffler won the PGA Tour's FedEx Cup Playoffs. But these guys won, too. The post 5 winners (besides Scottie Scheffler) from PGA Tour’s playoffs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Scottie Scheffler is the best golfer on the PGA Tour. That is the least interesting but most true sentence we’ll include here, but it’s worth establishing off the top; Scheffler reaffirmed his position atop the game at Sunday’s Tour Championship with a round of 66 that catapulted him past the 54-hole leaders and broke the collective spirit of every other player in contention.

Scheffler’s season had been notably strange because he finished second place five different times to five different very worthy opponents. But on Sunday he got the last laugh; for the second time in three weeks, he left all five in the dust. Jackson Koivun (who beat him at the 3M Open) was at home; his next shot at Scheffler will come in 2027. Matt Fitzpatrick (who beat him at the RBC Heritage) was well off the pace in a share of 21st. Cameron Young (who beat him at the Cadillac) was unable to summon any momentum en route to T11. Rory McIlroy (who beat him at the Masters) started too far back to challenge and finished T4. And Viktor Hovland (who beat him at the Travelers) began Sunday three shots ahead of Scheffler but finished three shots behind.

Golf.body: LIV Golf “may file for bankruptcy protection as soon as next week” as the circuit “races to find funding for a slimmed-down version slated for 2027,” according to sources cited by the FINANCIAL TIMES. The league “in recent days has sent settlement offers to the current LIV players who are owed millions in guaranteed payouts past 2026,” with those initial offers “at just a few cents on the dollar.” For several weeks, LIV has been “negotiating a funding package” with the credit division of private capital firm BC Partners, and BC executives have “attended recent LIV tournaments in Indiana and New Jersey to make their pitch to players.” LIV’s bankruptcy filing “may be made in the federal district court of New Jersey, a venue that is known to be friendly to debtors.” BC Partners, “while conducting due diligence, is itself waiting for LIV and PIF to resolve player payments and structure the bankruptcy terms” (FINANCIAL TIMES, 8/31).

Golf.body:
LIV Golf, the Saudi-backed challenger to the US PGA Tour, could file for bankruptcy within days, the Financial Times reported, as the kingdom shifts position on several high-profile projects.

Golf.title: Rose Zhang didn't win the FM Championship but she left with the next best thing
Golf.summary: As Rose Zhang tried to play her way onto the Solheim Cup team this year, one question followed her. She answered it at the FM Championship. The post Rose Zhang didn’t win the FM Championship but she left with the next best thing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rose Zhang knew this would be a weird year for her on the course after finishing up her Stanford degree in the spring. Transitioning back to being a full-time pro was going to have its bumps, but the former Stanford star faced it with one big goal in mind.

In two previous Solheim Cup appearances, Zhang went 4-2-1 and looked to cement herself as part of the backbone of future teams along with Nelly Korda. But after stepping back from full-time competitive golf to finish her degree at Stanford, Zhang’s world-class game was rusty and she knew she needed to prove herself to coach Angela Stanford to make the 2026 team. Zhang struggled in her return to full-time LPGA play earlier this year. She missed the cut at the JM LA Eagle Championsho and the Chevron Championship. After a T9 at the Ford in March, Zhang posted just one top-12 finish in her next 10 starts. She made the cut at the four majors after the Chevron but didn’t finish better than T41. As the calendar turned to August, Zhang had one thought as she tried to prove she should be Stanford’s team that will compete in the Netherlands during the second week of September.

Golf.title: Ruoning Yin returns to winner's circle with emotional victory in Boston
Golf.summary: After two years without a victory, Ruoning Yin rejoined the winner's circle Sunday at the FM Championship. The post Ruoning Yin returns to winner’s circle with emotional victory in Boston appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
NORTON, Mass. — After two years without a victory, Ruoning Yin finally had her moment again. Yin closed out a hard-fought final round Sunday at the FM Championship with a 2-under 70, including a two-putt birdie on the par-5 18th to win by two and capture the sixth LPGA Tour title of her career.

The victory was Yin’s first since 2024 and came after a week in which she repeatedly found herself battling for the lead with Hyo Joo Kim and Sei Young Kim. She stayed patient throughout the final round, even as the leaderboard shifted, and finished the week with 24 birdies—the most of any player in the field.

Golf.title: 'Never gave up': LPGA legend's emotional goodbye week ended with a message
Golf.summary: Anna Nordqvist's competitive career ended at the FM Championship. After a finishing par, she delivered a message. The post ‘Never gave up’: LPGA legend’s emotional goodbye week ended with a message appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Anna Nordqvist has always been wired to compete. You don’t win 16 times worldwide, including three majors, and make nine Solheim Cup teams without loving the grind and the fight. So, even as the 39-year-old, who announced Wednesday that she’d be retiring from competitive golf after this week’s FM Championship, was playing the final holes of a legendary career, she could only think about one thing.

“I’m a competitor. I don’t know how the putt doesn’t go in on eight or how the putt doesn’t go in on the last hole,” Nodqvist said on Sunday after shooting a final-round even-par 72 to finish T38.

Golf.title: England's Dean storms to British Masters title
Golf.summary: Former supermarket delivery driver Joe Dean fires a nine-under-par final-round to come from seven shots back to win his first DP World Tour title.
Golf.body:
Former supermarket delivery driver Joe Dean fired a sensational bogey-free nine-under-par 63 to snatch the British Masters title at The Belfry. It is a first DP World Tour victory in his 70th event for the 32-year-old Englishman who is ranked 292nd in the world.

He collected the trophy and about £440,000 in prize money, more than he had earned in total from his previous 19 tournaments in the 2026 season. "All those painful hours and all the work, it's finally led to something," said Dean, who two years ago was delivering groceries to help fund his golf.

Golf.title: 5 reasons every golfer should practice hitting balls off a tee
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel explains why hitting golf balls off a tee is a great way to practice your swing. The post 5 reasons every golfer should practice hitting balls off a tee appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of my favorite training aids when I teach is the simple golf tee. There are so many ways you can use a tee to help improve your motion and provide valuable feedback. Surprisingly, golfers often think it is a penalty to have to use a tee, but I strongly believe the opposite: you can use the tee to your advantage.

Here are five reasons I believe every golfer should practice hitting balls off a tee. Once you are into a full swing, it can be a great idea to start with a low tee to get the swing going without having to worry as much about hitting the ball and then the ground. Using the tee as feedback for where you are hitting the ground is very helpful. When swinging any club other than the driver, the tee should be hit and even broken if you are swinging with enough speed. Doing this during your warm-up can build confidence and help the rest of the day go better.

Golf.title: ‘I love you, dude’: Tiger Woods honored a friend. It was both touching and telling
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods’s most recent semi-public appearance came by way of a video message he made for childhood friend Notah Begay. The post ‘I love you, dude’: Tiger Woods honored a friend. It was both touching and telling appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The other day, Holly Finchem revealed to the golf-loving world, via Global Golf Post, that her husband, Tim Finchem, has Alzheimer’s. In his 22 years as PGA Tour commissioner — the Tiger Years, essentially — Finchem was always of sound mind and body. He was always a trim and fit man. But the former—his strategic and lawyerly brain — was his bread and butter, and now a disease with no known cure has settled in it.

Holly Finchem’s forthright and powerful commentary brought to mind the last time husband and wife, married for nearly 40 years, were at the center of golf’s spotlight, on a Wednesday night in March of 2022, on the eve of the Players Championship, when Finchem was inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame. Tiger Woods was the headliner that evening — he was inducted that night, too. Finchem and Woods sat next to one another for most of the night, in the first row of a space-age auditorium of the Tour’s new headquarters, its “Global Home,” per the Tour’s own branding. Finchem wrapped up his remarks by publicly thanking Holly “for agreeing to marry me.” It was both lawyerly and moving. It was a beautiful thing to say. Beautiful and easy.

Golf.title: Adam Scott's Tour Championship contention a reminder of pro golf's constant force
Golf.summary: Adam Scott's Tour Championship contention is a reminder of pro golf's main constant force and one thing that has kept it at bay. The post Adam Scott’s Tour Championship contention a reminder of pro golf’s constant force appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Twenty years ago this November, the PGA Tour’s Tour Championship was contested in early November. It was still held at East Lake Golf Club, but it was a time before the FedEx Cup, before the professional golf world as we know it began to take shape. A time before LIV Golf was born and (maybe?) died, before Brian Rolapp arrived and worked to reshape the PGA Tour’s postseason model from the FedEx Cup to a new iteration that will begin in 2028. That week, as the PGA Tour’s 30 best players were playing in Atlanta, Tom Brady threw four interceptions in a Sunday Night Football loss to Peyton Manning and the Indianapolis Colts. Brady would go on to play 16 more seasons, win four more Super Bowls and retire in 2022.

On that Sunday in 2006 at East Lake, Adam Scott defeated Jim Furyk to win the Tour Championship. A lot has changed about golf and the world since that November in 2006. Change has been a constant force in pro golf ever since Tiger Woods arrived, forever altering the sport, and it has only accelerated over the last decade. The money grows, the sponsors and tournaments and schedules shift and the players get younger and better.

Golf.title: At FM Championship, 1 major Solheim Cup question emerged
Golf.summary: Angel Yin returned to competition for the first time in two months at the FM Championship and brought a big Solheim Cup question with her. The post At FM Championship, 1 major Solheim Cup question emerged appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
FM Championship week began with U.S. captain Angela Stanford selecting Rose Zhang, Megan Khang and Lindy Duncan as the final three members of her team to travel to the Netherlands in two weeks. But while Stanford’s roster was technically completed on Monday, one big question remained.

One that took center stage during the first two days of the FM Championship at TPC Boston. Angel Yin, who made the U.S. Solheim Cup team on points, withdrew from the third round of the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship in June and hasn’t played since. Yin told Golfweek’s Beth Ann Nichols that she had stomach and gastrointestinal problems that caused her to lose 35 pounds. After two months away from competitive golf, Yin returned this week at the FM Championship for a trial run to see how her game feels and if she believes she’s fit to play in the Netherlands.

Golf.title: 'Pisses me off more': Viktor Hovland is lost (and in the lead) at Tour Championship

Golf.body:
UPDATE: Viktor Hovland birdied three of his final four holes to shoot a 65 in Round 3 and heads into Sunday’s final round of the Tour Championship with a one-shot lead. Golf.title: This clever training aid delivers instant ball-striking feedback
Golf.summary: Knowing your club path through impact is crucial for understanding your swing. For help with that, try the Divot Board. The post This clever training aid delivers instant ball-striking feedback appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Having an understanding of the direction your clubhead is moving through impact — the club path — is crucial for improving your ball striking. If you practice with a launch monitor, this information is easy to come by. For the rest of us? Not so much. One method is to look at your divot pattern in the turf during your practice sessions, but with not every practice facility offering real grass ranges, this isn’t an option for everyone.

If you face this dilemma, worry not — there’s a training aid designed to solve for just that. Enter the Divot Board. This portable training is designed to plop down anywhere you are practicing, allowing you to hit balls off the surface and giving you real-time feedback on how your clubhead is moving through impact. After each shot, you can clearly see on the board what direction your club is moving through impact, along with where the low point of your swing is — two crucial components for competent ball striking.

Srixon’s ZXi line of irons has been one of the more popular both on Tour and at retail since it debuted in 2025, and all indications are that the next iteration also will be well received.

Golf.title: Fleetwood in contention as Lee leads Tour Championship
Golf.summary: Defending champion Tommy Fleetwood shoots a four-under 66 to put himself in contention at the Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta.
Golf.body:
Defending champion Tommy Fleetwood shot a four-under 66 to put himself in contention, four strokes off first-round leader Min Woo Lee at the Tour Championship in Atlanta. However, Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy endured a mixed start in his bid to win a record-extending fourth Fedex Cup, bogeying two of the first four holes before fighting back on the back nine to sign for a 68.

Lee carded a bogey-free 62 to set the pace at eight under as he equalled his best round on the PGA Tour in its season-ending event at East Lake. Australia's Lee is two strokes clear of Norway's Viktor Hovland, who triumphed in 2023, and American duo Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup.

Golf.title: How golf's young stars finding motivation in one another
Golf.summary: Successful young Tour pros like Tommy Morrison have been finding motivation in the sparkling performances of their peers. The post How golf’s young stars finding motivation in one another appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
“The toughest opponent is old man par.” So said Bobby Jones nearly a century ago. Times have changed. Today’s young stars beat par with ease, routinely taking rounds deep into the red. They look for motivation in another opponent, but their greatest adversaries are also their peers.

“It’s pretty amazing what the young guys are doing,” Tommy Morrison said on a recent episode of GOLF’s Subpar podcast. At 22, Morrison is a young guy himself who has rocketed to success since making his Korn Ferry Tour debut this year. He tied for 10th in his first start, followed that with a fifth and a runner-up finish before breaking through with a victory at the Evans Scholars Invitational. He added another runner-up finish the following week.

Golf.title: Callaway nixes Good Good partnership after driver-ad fallout
Golf.summary: Callaway Golf has severed ties with Good Good Golf following a controversial ad promoting a collaborative driver. The post Callaway nixes Good Good partnership after driver-ad fallout appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Less than a week after Callaway and Good Good Golf removed an ad for a collaborative driver that featured a man pushing a woman to the ground, the two companies are no longer working together.

Callaway announced Thursday it has ended its relationship with Good Good, a YouTube Golf giant with over two million subscribers, effective immediately. In a statement provided to GOLF, Callaway said it had completed its review of the matter involving a promotional ad created by Good Good for a branded collaborative Callaway Quantum driver and taken additional actions to strengthen their content review process. The company also said it was committing $1 million to support organizations working to prevent violence against women, provide resources to survivors and advance education and awareness efforts.

Golf.title: Good Good and Callaway made a mistake. Now they’re paying the price
Golf.summary: Good Good and Callaway have been in damage-control mode. We asked three crisis-communications experts to assess the brands’ tactics. The post Good Good and Callaway made a mistake. Now they’re paying the price appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Good Good and Callaway Golf knew they had a problem. As a jarring clip of their short-lived, now-infamous driver ad began circulating on social media Friday, the blowback was swift, widespread and unrelenting. How, legions of commenters wondered — many angrily — could these companies possibly have produced, approved and published a video that depicted a man (Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark) shoving a woman (Clark’s fellow Good Good creator, Alexis Miestowski) to the ground?

Whatever your virtual town square of choice — X, Facebook, Tiktok, Reddit — you could find scores of critics decrying the spot as, among other things, tasteless, insensitive and tone deaf (commenter remark: “Threw my Good Good hat in the garbage”). Which isn’t to say everyone was aghast. You didn’t have to scroll long to find observers who thought the video was, if not cinematic genius, no big deal (commenter remark, written facetiously: “How many woman [sic] will be harmed because of the @goodgood_golf add?” [sic]).

Golf.title: We toured Mitsubishi's new state-of-the-art Carlsbad HQ. It was a long time coming
Golf.summary: Mitsubishi Golf Shafts has been a leader in the industry for decades, but they've never had a home for testing in the US. That's all changed. The post We toured Mitsubishi’s new state-of-the-art Carlsbad HQ. It was a long time coming appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Mitsubishi Golf Shafts is a juggernaut in the golf shaft world, and its headquarters now reflects that. They’re one of the only companies that are completely vertically integrated, meaning they manufacture the material themselves and they’ve driven major trends in the shaft industry for decades.

But until recently, their U.S. HQ has never really been anything to brag about, at least not for experiential testing, research, prototyping development, and ideation. That’s all changed with the opening of the brand-new Mitsubishi KOBO Studio inside their Carlsbad, Calif. headquarters.

Golf.title: Famed architect starts scholarship for aspiring course designers
Golf.summary: In 1982, Tom Doak won a scholarship that helped shape his career in course design. He's now helped fund a similar award in his name. The post Famed architect starts scholarship for aspiring course designers appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In 1982, as a 21-year-old undergraduate at Cornell University, Tom Doak won a scholarship that he put toward travel and research overseas. Cornell’s Dreer Award was earmarked for students of landscape architecture, a major Doak had chosen because it was the closest the school offered to the field in which he hoped to work. He dreamed of becoming a golf-course architect.

With $10,000 in support, Doak spent nine months visiting 170 courses across the United Kingdom and Ireland, developing an eye and understanding of design that have since propelled him to industry renown. (In 1987, another aspiring course architect, Doak’s future peer Gil Hanse, won the Dreer Award, too.)

Golf.title: Maguire makes steady start at Women's Irish Open
Golf.summary: Leona Maguire's latest bid for a first Women's Irish Open title began in steady fashion as she carded a one-under 71 in Thursday's first round at the K Club.
Golf.body:
Leona Maguire's latest bid for a first Women's Irish Open title began in steady fashion as she carded a one-under 71 in Thursday's first round at the K Club. The 31-year-old, who was selected as one of European captain Anna Nordqvist's Solheim Cup wildcard picks earlier this month, carded three birdies and two bogeys to sit eight shots off breakaway leader Casandra Alexander of South Africa.

Maguire, who has missed 11 of 19 cuts this season, birdied two of the four par-fives and also picked up a shot at the par-three second - her 11th hole - with dropped shots at the sixth and 16th holes.

Golf.title: Everyone has a 'Dream 18'. We made ours a reality
Golf.summary: What started as a wacky golf hypothetical turned into a 15-hour round like we never imagined. We brought our Dream 18 to life. The post Everyone has a ‘Dream 18’. We made ours a reality appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
DOOR COUNTY, Wisconsin — As we kicked around his living room looking for any sign of life, it became clear that Keith Mann was missing. And we needed him for the longest golf round of our lives.

Our foursome had risen early. We’d played five hours of golf already and had at least another seven hours ahead of us. Mann’s rough-and-tumble 9-holer, Top of the Door, was our sixth course of the day, squarely in the middle of our “Dream 18.” It was also the only course bound by the schedule of Madonna, a car ferry connecting tiny Washington Island, Wis., to the rest of its mitten-shaped mainland.

Golf.title: 'That's fuel': With successful major season behind her, Nelly Korda still eyes 1 goal
Golf.summary: A dream-achieving season hasn't left Nelly Korda complacent. While the major year is over, she still has one main goal on her mind. The post ‘That’s fuel’: With successful major season behind her, Nelly Korda still eyes 1 goal appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Nelly Korda’s 2026 season has been an emphatic response to her winless 2025 campaign. She’s relied on a new mindset and an on-course freedom that she has connected to her off-course happiness, maturity and a competitive drive that received unlimited fuel after 2025. It’s been effective.

Korda opened her season with a win. Then she won the first major of the year in emphatic fashion and followed that up by achieving a lifelong dream, winning the U.S. Women’s Open at Riviera. On the heels of that blistering start, the LPGA created a “scrappy” marketing plan to introduce Korda to a larger sports audience and bring in new eyeballs to the sport as she readied for the year’s final three majors and a chance to punch her ticket to the LPGA Hall of Fame. Korda’s season leveled off after that. Her putter went cold at the KPMG Women’s PGA, she missed the cut at the Evian and was one of many players to let a golden opportunity slip through her fingers at the AIG Women’s Open.

Golf.title: LIV Golf tells 90% of staff they will lose their jobs next week
Golf.summary: LIV Golf tells 90% of staff they will lose their jobs next week Golfmagic
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is set to lose around 90% of its workforce next week as the league dramatically scales back its operations. Staff were reportedly told on Monday that the majority of employees will leave the organisation in the first week of September, despite many already receiving 30-day termination notices earlier this month.

The scale of the cuts are said to have come as a shock to some employees, with LIV employing approximately 300 people across its London and New York offices. According to Telegraph Sport, senior executives are expected to remain, alongside a skeleton workforce with only a small number of employees retained in some departments.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy applauds TaylorMade's Qi4D driver decision
Golf.summary: At the Tour Championship, Rory McIlroy explained why he and other pros are excited about TaylorMade moving to a two-year driver cycle. The post Rory McIlroy applauds TaylorMade’s Qi4D driver decision appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy has a driver he likes and he’s looking forward to playing it for the foreseeable future. And why is this significant? Glad you asked. In May, McIlroy’s equipment sponsor, TaylorMade, announced it was moving to a two-year product cycle for its metal woods starting with the Qi4D family released last January. With the move, TaylorMade became the fourth of the six largest OEMs in the sport to move its metalwoods to a two-year product cycle, joining Ping, Srixon and Titleist. As of now, Callaway and Cobra have yet to share any intentions of moving off a yearly release cadence for their drivers.

“I think being able to use the same driver for say like an 18-month period I think just gives guys a little bit more of a level of comfort,” McIlroy said Tuesday at the Tour Championship.

Golf.title: Three-time major winner Nordqvist announces retirement
Golf.summary: Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist will retire from professional golf after this week's FM Championship near Boston.
Golf.body:
Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist will retire from professional golf after this week's FM Championship near Boston. Nordqvist, 39, will captain Europe at Bernardus Golf in Netherlands, when they take on the United States on 11-13 September in the Solheim Cup.

The Swede has featured in each of the previous nine editions of the biennial contest, helping Europe lift the trophy on five occasions since making her debut in 2009. That was the same year Nordqvist enjoyed her first major success at the LPGA Championship and she also triumphed at the Evian Championship in 2017 and the Women's Open in 2021.

Golf.title: LIV Golf to lay off majority of staff amid ‘compressed timeline’ for new investors
Golf.summary: LIV Golf to lay off majority of staff amid ‘compressed timeline’ for new investors The Guardian
Golf.body:
LIV Golf informed the majority of its workforce on Wednesday that they will be laid off in the first week of September. The news comes three days after the 2026 season concluded in Indianapolis and four months after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund announced it was ending its financial support of the league after spending more than $5bn over the past five years.

Wednesday’s announcement to staff was not unexpected after the tour notified workers in the US and the UK of potential layoffs. The LIV Golf chief executive, Scott O’Neil, is working to finalise a deal with a new lead investor to fund a re-imagined LIV 2.0. However, the league faces an uncertain future, with the season-ending team championship in Michigan cancelled, the purse for the Indianapolis event slashed nearly in half, multiple vendors still awaiting payments and the potential for bankruptcy looming.

Golf.body:
American golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended for six months for betting on golf tournaments, the PGA Tour has said. The 55-year-old competes on the PGA Tour Champions circuit which is reserved for professional golfers aged 50 and older.

Gogel did not bet on events in which he was participating but admitted to unknowingly violating PGA Tour policy by placing "small recreational wagers" in 2024 and 2025. "I would never knowingly violate the integrity of the game of golf," Gogel said in a statement.

Golf.title: PGA Tour Champions pro is suspended 6 months for betting on Tour events

Golf.body:
Matt Gogel, a member of the PGA Tour Champions circuit, has been suspended six months by the PGA Tour for betting on Tour events. The bets violated the Tour’s “Integrity Program,” and Gogel’s suspension started Sunday. A statement from Gogel, which was provided by the PGA Tour on Wednesday, said that he wagered on events in which he did not play, and that the bets came in 2024 and ’25.

“In 2024 and 2025, I unknowingly violated the PGA Tour policy by placing small, recreational wagers on golf,” Gogel’s statement said. “I want to be clear that these wagers were not placed on regular PGA Tour events, PGA Tour Champions events or any tournament in which I participated.

Golf.title: 'Pretty weak': Nick Faldo sees a dim future for LIV Golf 2.0
Golf.summary: As LIV Golf teeters on the edge, Nick Faldo doesn't see the breakaway league having a bright future even if version 2.0 gets off the ground. The post ‘Pretty weak’: Nick Faldo sees a dim future for LIV Golf 2.0 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LIV Golf 1.0 ended on Sunday in Indianapolis with an odd scene that perfectly captured the chaos that has enveloped the league since the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund announced it was withdrawing funding from the outfit after the 2026 season. There was Jon Rahm evading questions about his future, Tyrrell Hatton trying to run to the airport and Bryson DeChambeau trying, and failing, to project confidence in LIV 2.0.

Last week, LIV CEO Scott O’Neil told the press he was bullish on where LIV was headed in its new era — one that will involve a shorter schedule, smaller purses and more player control in how the league is run. O’Neil has been trying to steady the ship, including securing an agreement from an outside investor. But with some of LIV’s biggest names reportedly looking to head for the exit, the breakaway league is teetering.

Golf.body:

At the start of this year a small number of LIV players were given a path back to the PGA Tour with a three-week deadline to accept the invitation on the “returning members programme”, which was used by Brooks Koepka in January.

Golf.title: Tim Finchem fought for the PGA Tour. Now he’s fighting a different battle
Golf.summary: Tim Finchem, who shrewdly governed the PGA Tour for more than two decades, has been battling Alzheimer’s disease. The post Tim Finchem fought for the PGA Tour. Now he’s fighting a different battle appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Alzheimer’s disease has settled into the minds of tens of millions of people around the world, and it’s likely you’ve seen it up close in your own life. It doesn’t discriminate. Holly Finchem, in her beautiful comments to Global Golf Post about her husband, former PGA Tour commissioner Tim Finchem, made that point without even trying. Here was — here is — a man who, as people often say mindlessly, has it all: family, career, financial security, intelligence, a disciplined manner of living, good work-life balance and good health. Good health until he didn’t. Mrs. Finchem said it so powerfully: What ALS does to the body, Alzheimer’s does to the brain.

This guy had some mind. At press conferences and interviews, he ran circles around reporters, responding to our simple and direct questions with a long minute or two of gobbledygook, appearing to say everything while saying nothing, because it didn’t serve his purposes. Tim Finchem was a lawyer with a keen understanding of the nation’s capital and an uncanny ability to play things close to the vest. As the PGA Tour’s third commissioner — he had the job from the middle of 1994 to the end of 2016 — he was always playing poker.

Golf.body:
Brian Rolapp is nothing if not consistent and on message. When the PGA Tour CEO opened the door for Brooks Koepka to come back from LIV Golf in January through the “Returning Member Program,” he made one thing clear.

“This is a one-time, defined window and does not set a precedent for future situations,” Rolapp said in the announcement that Koepka was returning. “Once the door closes, there is no promise that this path will be available again.”

Golf.title: How this golfer dropped her scores from the 90s to the low 80s
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tony Ruggiero details the progress of a student who dramatically dropped her scoring average. The post How this golfer dropped her scores from the 90s to the low 80s appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Anna is the kind of student every coach loves to work with. She played college tennis before she ever got serious about golf, and when she came back to the game as a mid-amateur, she brought that same competitiveness with her. In just over a year and a half of real work, her scores have come down from the 90s into the low 80s, with a few rounds even lower than that. That kind of jump doesn’t happen from a swing tip or two. It happens from a plan.

Morgan Hale, the director of instruction at The Creek, has been building that plan with Anna since the start. Foundational work on posture, on club face and path through the wedges, and on structure at the top of the swing. I get folded in for what we call our “performance sessions,” where I’ll join Morgan and PGA Tour trainer Kolby Tullier to combine golf instruction and fitness in the same lesson.

Golf.title: Ian Poulter Casts Doubt on LIV Golf Future With Latest Admission
Golf.summary: Ian Poulter Casts Doubt on LIV Golf Future With Latest Admission dailyclubgolf.com
Golf.body:
As the whole LIV 2.0 scene hangs by a thread, 50-year-old professional golfer Ian Poulter had some feelings to let off his chest. “It would be a real shame if LIV 2.0 doesn’t happen,” he took to Instagram this Monday. “There are players who would love a strong global platform to play on… Some players will stay, some may go. As for me, I may stay or take some time off. I genuinely haven’t decided yet.”

This heartfelt admission came after the early end of the LIV campaign in Indianapolis on August 23, as they lost the financial support of the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia (PIF). Poulter didn’t mince his words, calling it “the doors (closing) on LIV Golf 1.0.”

Golf.title: Good Good ad and the initial response criticized by PGA Tour CEO
Golf.summary: A controversial Good Good ad and the initial response to it were criticized by PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp at this week's Tour Championship. The post Good Good ad and the initial response criticized by PGA Tour CEO appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
A controversial and since-deleted video ad for a driver developed by Good Good and Callaway Golf was “concerning,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp says. Rolapp also said the initial response to it was “disappointing,” and that “it’s a bit of a fluid situation” in answering a question about the status of Good Good, a YouTube content group, in the Good Good Championship, a PGA Tour event set for Nov. 12-15.

Rolapp’s comments, coming Tuesday ahead of the Tour Championship, were his first publicly since the release of the ad and the fallout from it. In a portion of the video, Good Good’s Garrett Clark runs toward Alexis Miestowski, another member of Good Good, after she reaches for the club, and he pushes her. Miestowski then screams before Clark stands over her and says: “Do not touch my new driver.”

, players weighed every word as carefully as their drop shots. But beyond the glare of the cameras, another contest was quietly unfolding. Standing a step behind the athletes were the interpreters, almost invisible yet carrying the immense responsibility of ensuring that nuance survived the journey from Mandarin, Japanese or Korean into English.

At a World Championships, where every word can travel as quickly as a smash, a mistranslated phrase can soften conviction, distort the meaning of an entire exchange or, in the worst case, trigger an unintended geopolitical controversy. For the interpreters, getting the words right is only part of the job. The real challenge is ensuring that nothing gets lost in translation.

Badminton.title: World Championships Review: Memorable Matches
Badminton.summary: World Championships Review: Memorable Matches BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
For sheer edge-of-the-seat action, this was the standout match. That it featured two unknown pairs made it all the more fascinating. World No.60 Surya and Pramuthesh, promoted from the reserves, took on No.72 Sonmez/Bektas and it was a thriller all the way, with the Turkiye pair fighting off seven match points in the second game and two in the third.

This was reckoned to be the highlight of the opening day, and it lived up to expectations. Fast-rising youngster Shetty had a great start against the defending champion; but Shi took the match to a decider. With Shetty leading 17-6 it looked all but over for the top seed, but Shi staged a magnificent comeback and nearly took the match, and it needed all of Shetty’s composure to nail the last few points for one of the significant upsets in World Championships history.

Badminton.title: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joonas Korhonen
Badminton.summary: Humans of Shuttle Time: Joonas Korhonen BWF Fansite
Badminton.body:
This is the 72nd story in our Humans of Shuttle Time series, in which we present the perspectives of those who are involved with badminton at the grassroots level. Joonas Korhonen, Shuttle Time Tutor with Finnish Badminton Federation, talks of his journey in badminton.

I was into sports since I was a very little kid. I always played different sports outdoors with my dad and older kids. I never enjoyed studying, but I still pushed myself through high school. My best memories are from the sports high school where I was able to play badminton three mornings in a week and it was part of the school programme.

Badminton.title: World Championships: Key Takeaways
Badminton.summary: World Championships: Key Takeaways BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
France as a badminton power isn’t news anymore – their silver at the BWF Thomas Cup Finals earlier this year was definitive proof. Yet, their two-gold finish in New Delhi underlined how staggeringly far they’ve come, for, after the inaugural edition of the World Championships in 1977 when Denmark won three gold, no European nation had won more than one gold at a particular edition.

This achievement has a sub-text: Denmark has been overtaken by another European power. France’s depth in men’s singles, which served them so well in the Thomas Cup, was again in evidence at the World Championships. Alex Lanier was one of three prospects; Christo Popov was the frontline French contender given his victory at the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2025 last December and the DAIHATSU Japan Open in July. Despite his loss in the opening round, and his brother Toma Junior’s in the Round of 16, that France did go on to win the men’s singles title showcased their depth.

Badminton.title: "I Am Proud Of A Country That Opened Its Heart To The World": BWF President After New Delhi 2026 World Championships
Badminton.summary: "I Am Proud Of A Country That Opened Its Heart To The World": BWF President After New Delhi 2026 World Championships Sportscape Magazine
Badminton.body:
BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul praised India's hosting of the BWF World Championships 2026 in New Delhi as a landmark week for world badminton. BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul has praised India’s hosting of the BWF World Championships 2026 following the event's conclusion on 23rd August. In a heartfelt message, the president expressed appreciation for a week in Delhi, the organizers, the people behind the scenes, and the players, according to the latest sports news from Indian badminton.

India hosted its last BWF World Championships in 2009 in Hyderabad, which means the tournament returns to India after 17 long years. Acknowledging that gap, the BWF President said, "What a week New Delhi has given us. India waited 17 years for this moment, and India made every year count. The BWF World Championships 2026 have won praise from every corner of our . That praise belongs to the people, and I would like to name them."

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: Treesa Jolly & Gayatri Gopichand storm into women’s doubles semifinals
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: Treesa Jolly & Gayatri Gopichand storm into women’s doubles semifinals News On AIR
Badminton.body: In Badminton, India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have stormed into the women’s doubles semifinals of the BWF World Championships in New Delhi. The Indian duo displayed remarkable grit and fighting spirit, coming from a game down to overcome fourth seeds Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian of China 16-21, 21-15, 21-13. With this triumph, Treesa and Gayatri have assured India of a coveted medal at the prestigious championship. This will be India’s first medal in the women’s doubles event at the World Championships in 15 years.

Badminton.title: Jonatan Christie Takes Top Spot
Badminton.summary: Jonatan Christie Takes Top Spot BWF
Badminton.body:
Jonatan Christie became the first Indonesian men’s singles player in over 25 years to take the top spot of the BWF World Rankings. Christie followed in the footsteps of his predecessor Taufik Hidayat, who was world No.1 between 2000 and 2001.

The Indonesian climbed two spots to supplant former world champion Shi Yu Qi, who slipped five places to No.6 after suffering a first round loss at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi last week.
